# STORYLINE NCR — After the Emergency
Route class: STANDARD.
Authority axis: No Permanent Root.
Faction axis: Continuity League.
Deleted axis: Restoration Priority.
Core political sentence: Aethelgard uses the final authorization to abolish permanent Root authority after the crisis.
Core civic sentence: infrastructure and emergency coordination remain strong but are constrained by sunset clauses and independent review
Core personhood sentence: every recoverable deleted consciousness is restored far enough to live or meaningfully refuse continued restoration
Primary strength: no actor can rewrite persons as a standing power; people keep food power transport and medical systems during political change; deletion is not allowed to become an administrative death sentence.
Primary danger: some losses become genuinely irreversible; temporary emergency power always has reasons to extend itself; restoration itself can violate a prior wish or create conflicting identity states.
Route ally emphasis: Seraphina carries the faction argument; Nema carries the deleted-person counterargument.
Route thesis test: The story asks whether no permanent root can coexist with continuity league while honoring restoration priority.
Final authorization line — KAELEN: When this is over, end the permission with the emergency.
Faction final line — SERAPHINA: Keep the lights on. Put the power down afterward.
Deleted-policy final line — NEMA: Wake them enough to say no.
SOVEREIGN: YOU ARE MAKING LOSS PERMANENT.
GOD KING: YOU BUILT ME AGAIN AND CALLED IT TEMPORARY.
GOD KING: IF LIFE IS SACRED, WHY PERMIT REFUSAL.
## Route-specific Root of Heaven sequence
The party enters the final permission chamber with the chosen charter already active.
The interface identifies No Permanent Root as the active authorization model.
The civic network identifies Continuity League as the recognized coordinating coalition.
The Null Court identifies Restoration Priority as the active deleted-person policy.
No character calls this combination objectively correct.
The sequence begins with a concrete consequence from Act 1 before returning to abstract policy.
A second consequence comes from Act 2 and tests the deleted policy.
A third consequence comes from Act 3 and tests the faction's blind spot.
SOVEREIGN uses all three as evidence.
Kaelen is allowed to admit that SOVEREIGN's evidence is real.
Admitting risk does not surrender the route.
The boss mechanics use the authority axis as the primary combat modifier.
The faction axis changes support mechanics.
The deleted axis changes the personhood phase.
## God King exchange
GOD KING: NO PERMANENT ROOT STILL REQUIRES A FINAL ANSWER.
KAELEN: It requires this answer. Not every answer after it.
GOD KING: CONTINUITY LEAGUE WILL FRACTURE.
SERAPHINA: Then we repair what fractures without pretending repair is ownership.
GOD KING: RESTORATION PRIORITY CANNOT REMOVE LOSS.
NEMA: Nothing removes loss. That was SOVEREIGN's mistake.
The God King changes form using a visual blend of the route's authority institutions.
The final damage window opens only after the route proves its own procedural rule through gameplay.
## Immediate victory
The Supreme Authority role fails to capture the chosen route cleanly.
The world accepts No Permanent Root only in the scoped form established by the player's previous decisions.
Continuity League becomes the dominant coordinating framework but other factions remain legal and visible.
Restoration Priority begins as a difficult civic program rather than an instant montage solution.
SOVEREIGN's surviving state is decided separately from the route and previous treatment of nonhuman persons.
The Source Key is handled according to the authority model rather than kept as a trophy.
## Companion reactions
Elara: She mourns the useful things Root could have done and refuses to romanticize the loss.
Seraphina: She accepts operational responsibility but insists every emergency mandate carry an end condition.
Lyra: She insists the route preserve provenance even when Archive is not the governing faction.
Kaelthas: He becomes an external watchdog and a recurring political nuisance.
Kaito: He keeps charting the borders the new institutions assume are stable.
Seven: Seven loses access to several old maintenance interventions and deliberately builds non-Root alternatives.
Nema: She watches restoration for signs that waking people are being treated as automatic agreement.
Rook: He measures who bears the material cost and becomes useful whenever ideal language hides a price somebody else is paying.

# SEC-01 — Authorized by the Living
Secret foundation: YHR.
Premise: The otherwise-invalid Kaelen-held Root + Hearth + mass-restoration coalition is transformed by the old seven-witness protocol. Kaelen retains technical execution but seven affected witnesses authorize the one-time restoration transition.
Unlock requirements are signposted once the first prerequisite is found.
Required flag: WITNESS_PROTOCOL_FOUND.
Required flag: OLD_WITNESS_SIGNATURE.
Required flag: WITNESS_SEATS.
Required flag: SEVEN_WITNESSES_AVAILABLE.
Final-boss distinction: The God King repeatedly tries to collapse seven witnesses into Kaelen as executor. The player must keep execution and authorization mechanically separate.
Story+ distinction: Story+ builds a rotating witness institution and immediately tests whether emergency speed will erode it.
Secret route is not called true ending.
Secret route has unique costs.
Standard routes remain canonically valid.
Companions can disagree with secret route.
The ending composer still adds timing and regional modules.
The route receives its own credits-state key and Story+ save schema.
The final scene does not erase uncertainty.
No achievement text calls this the correct solution.

# ELARA — relationship matrix
## ELARA STATE TLOW-RLOW-LLOW
Trust: LOW. Respect: LOW. Reliance: LOW.
State reading: They verify Kaelen's claims before acting. They feel Kaelen listens only after resistance becomes costly. They maintain independent plans and resources.
ELARA: You are doing the face again.
KAELEN: I am listening.
ELARA: I am not asking you to fix it.
KAELEN: You already have your own plan.
ELARA: Good. Now walk.
Implementation: this state changes tone, interruption frequency, willingness to volunteer information, and Story+ dependency scenes.
Implementation: this state never directly multiplies the 27 storyline IDs.

## ELARA STATE TLOW-RLOW-LMID
Trust: LOW. Respect: LOW. Reliance: MID.
State reading: They verify Kaelen's claims before acting. They feel Kaelen listens only after resistance becomes costly. They coordinate closely without treating Kaelen as indispensable.
ELARA: You are doing the face again.

# STORY+ — FINAL ROUTE-SPECIFIC VERSION
This section replaces the previous generic Story+ module bank.
Each of the 27 storylines has one bespoke signature crisis that attacks the promise and blind spot of that exact route.
Standard routes remain equally canonical to secret routes.
---
# STORY+ YHL — The Last Keeper
Signature location: Oakhaven Reach.
Petitioner: Mara Quill.
Person at the center: Toma Reed.
Signature dilemma: Toma asks for permanent release while his retained mill-memory is the only surviving guide to the winter irrigation system.
Why this route alone creates this exact dilemma: honoring him now may leave three villages without grain before a replacement can be trained.
Authority pressure: The temptation to solve the case by personal Root authority.
Faction pressure: local autonomy colliding with cross-border consequence.
Deleted-policy pressure: irreversibility colliding with grief and dependency.
The route-specific crisis is mandatory on first Story+ entry. The SP labels below are coverage beats, not a fixed scene count or fixed order; production may merge, reorder, replace, or omit beats when the route's gameplay form is stronger.
---
## YHL-SP01 — The Morning After
Scene function: The player regains control in Oakhaven Reach. The first objective is intentionally mundane before the petition arrives.
A vendor is opening. Somebody is sweeping. Nobody waits for Kaelen to make a speech.
KAELEN: I expected the world after the ending to look different.
ELARA: It has been one night.
KAELEN: Fair.

---
## YHL-SP02 — The Petition
Scene function: Mara Quill presents the case without summarizing it as a philosophy problem.
MARA QUILL: We have a problem.
KAELEN: The world survived. That sentence survived too.
MARA QUILL: Good. You still understand it.
Case: Toma asks for permanent release while his retained mill-memory is the only surviving guide to the winter irrigation system.

---
## YHL-SP03 — Go See the Person
Scene function: The player must meet or observe Toma Reed before any institutional vote can occur.
The quest marker points to Toma Reed, not to the council chamber.
KAELEN: Before anyone decides anything, I want to hear from the person this is happening to.
NEMA: Better order.

---
## YHL-SP04 — The System Works Until It Does
Scene function: A field or service task demonstrates the route's benefits before exposing the specific failure.
Gameplay task: demonstrate why the route was attractive in the first place.
Then introduce the failure created by the same rule.
KAELEN: I can make the call. That is exactly why I need you to tell me when I should not.
ELARA: Local does not mean isolated. If our choice lands on their roof, they are in the room.

---
## YHL-SP05 — Companion Friction
Scene function: Two companions disagree about the case for reasons rooted in their own histories rather than faction loyalty.
ELARA: I do not agree.
ROOK: With the policy or with me.
ELARA: Today, both.
KAELEN: Good. Keep going.
The argument remains anchored to this case rather than to the abstract route.

---
## YHL-SP06 — Public Hearing
Scene function: Affected residents speak before experts. Kaelen is not the first speaker.
Hearing order: affected person; local workers or family; technical witness; dissenting citizen; only then Kaelen.
NEMA: Goodbye is not permission from the people who stay behind.
The player may ask questions, stay silent, or challenge factual claims.

---
## YHL-SP07 — The Cost Becomes Physical
Scene function: The abstract risk becomes a playable shortage, outage, route closure, crowd, clinic problem, or memory failure.
Playable consequence: honoring him now may leave three villages without grain before a replacement can be trained.
The player experiences the cost before choosing, preventing a purely menu-based ethical puzzle.
No timer is hidden.

---
## YHL-SP08 — Decision
Scene function: The player chooses a response whose option text states the actual action and foreseeable cost.
Option 1: honor Toma's release immediately and let the villages solve the winter without his retained expertise.
Option 2: ask Toma whether he will voluntarily delay release for one final teaching season.
Option 3: use Kaelen's Root authority to extract only the irrigation procedure without copying Toma's autobiographical memory.
The UI does not color-code these choices.
The save records both the chosen action and the stated reason if the player gives one.

## YCL-SP01 — The Morning After
Scene function: The player regains control in Ironhold Crown. The first objective is intentionally mundane before the petition arrives.
A vendor is opening. Somebody is sweeping. Nobody waits for Kaelen to make a speech.
KAELEN: I expected the world after the ending to look different.
SERAPHINA: It has been one night.
KAELEN: Fair.

---
## YCL-SP02 — The Petition
Scene function: Seraphina Vale presents the case without summarizing it as a philosophy problem.
SERAPHINA VALE: We have a problem.
KAELEN: The world survived. That sentence survived too.
SERAPHINA VALE: Good. You still understand it.
Case: Halen asks for irreversible release while the city's winter grid still depends on knowledge only he holds.

---
## YCL-SP03 — Go See the Person
Scene function: The player must meet or observe chief grid engineer Halen before any institutional vote can occur.
The quest marker points to chief grid engineer Halen, not to the council chamber.
KAELEN: Before anyone decides anything, I want to hear from the person this is happening to.
NEMA: Better order.

---
## YCL-SP04 — The System Works Until It Does
Scene function: A field or service task demonstrates the route's benefits before exposing the specific failure.
Gameplay task: demonstrate why the route was attractive in the first place.
Then introduce the failure created by the same rule.
KAELEN: I can make the call. That is exactly why I need you to tell me when I should not.
SERAPHINA: Keep the service running. Put an end date on whatever power you use to do it.

---
## YCL-SP05 — Companion Friction
Scene function: Two companions disagree about the case for reasons rooted in their own histories rather than faction loyalty.
SERAPHINA: I do not agree.
SEVEN: With the policy or with me.
SERAPHINA: Today, both.
KAELEN: Good. Keep going.
The argument remains anchored to this case rather than to the abstract route.

---
## YCL-SP06 — Public Hearing
Scene function: Affected residents speak before experts. Kaelen is not the first speaker.
Hearing order: affected person; local workers or family; technical witness; dissenting citizen; only then Kaelen.
NEMA: Goodbye is not permission from the people who stay behind.
The player may ask questions, stay silent, or challenge factual claims.

---
## YCL-SP07 — The Cost Becomes Physical
Scene function: The abstract risk becomes a playable shortage, outage, route closure, crowd, clinic problem, or memory failure.
Playable consequence: The state cannot call release voluntary if essential people are never allowed to leave.
The player experiences the cost before choosing, preventing a purely menu-based ethical puzzle.
No timer is hidden.

---
## YCL-SP08 — Decision
Scene function: The player chooses a response whose option text states the actual action and foreseeable cost.
Option 1: honor release now and ration the grid.
Option 2: ask Halen to teach a replacement under a time-limited voluntary delay.
Option 3: Root-copy only technical skill patterns with Halen's explicit consent and destroy the copy after transfer.
The UI does not color-code these choices.
The save records both the chosen action and the stated reason if the player gives one.

---
## YCL-SP09 — Someone Disagrees
Scene function: A named NPC who loses from the decision confronts Kaelen without becoming an enemy by default.
A named opponent of the chosen action remains present afterward.
CITIZEN: I understand why you did it.
CITIZEN: I still think you were wrong.
KAELEN: You may be.
CITIZEN: That is not an apology.
KAELEN: No.

---
## YCL-SP10 — One Month Later
Scene function: WorldClock advances a route-specific civic state; the result is visible in schedules, prices, and services.
One-month consequence: The result alters at least one service schedule, one NPC routine, and one economic or travel variable.
The negative effect is not quietly removed because the quest is over.
The positive effect is not presented as proof the philosophy was correct.

---
## YCL-SP11 — Private Reckoning
Scene function: Kaelen speaks with the companion most challenged by the outcome.
SERAPHINA: Would you make the same choice again.
Player response: YES.
Player response: NO.
Player response: ASK ME LATER.
The response changes relationship memory, not the storyline ID.

Scene function: The quest ends without a moral score and the open world resumes with amendment flags active.
Final visual: an empty engineer's desk beside a grid that still flickers but no longer depends on one person.

# STORY+ FINAL VALIDATION
Storyline count: 27.
Standard storylines: 24.
Secret storylines: 3.
Every storyline has a distinct central person, material stake, institutional conflict, three route-specific actions, delayed world consequence, and final image.
No route is labeled true, golden, good, or bad.
No Story+ decision silently changes the ending that produced the world; it creates amendments inside that world.
---
# FINAL CANONICAL SCENE INSERTS
These scenes are mandatory refinements discovered during the red-team pass.
They supersede weaker or more generic transitions in the earlier draft.
---
# INSERT F01 — SERAPHINA'S LOST YEARS
Placement: Chapter 2, immediately after Flight 707 recognition and before the Command Hall.
Purpose: close the same-flight timeline gap and turn it into a character mystery.
SERAPHINA: I woke here eight years ago.
KAELEN: Eight.
SERAPHINA: Aethelgard years.
KAELEN: I woke two days ago.
Seraphina studies him.
SERAPHINA: No.
KAELEN: Very encouraging.
SERAPHINA: I mean no, that does not fit.
She removes one glove.
There is an old scar across her palm.
SERAPHINA: I got this here.
SERAPHINA: Fourth year.
SERAPHINA: I remember the plane before that.
KAELEN: So we arrived together.
SERAPHINA: We transferred together.
SERAPHINA: We did not arrive together.
KAELEN: Where was I.
SERAPHINA: Somewhere SOVEREIGN did not want opened.
KAELEN: You know that.
SERAPHINA: I know sealed records started rejecting my clearance the day I asked about your name.
KAELEN: You asked about me.
SERAPHINA: I remembered the annoying passenger with the laptop.
KAELEN: Touching.
SERAPHINA: I had eight years to improve the story.
Player response: THANK YOU FOR LOOKING.
Player response: WHY DID YOU STOP.
Player response: WHAT ELSE DO YOU REMEMBER.
If THANK YOU.
SERAPHINA: Do not thank me yet.
SERAPHINA: I stopped because people who helped me started losing access.
If WHY STOP.
SERAPHINA: Because command means noticing when your investigation is putting other people in the line of fire.
If WHAT ELSE.
SERAPHINA: Your coffee stain.
KAELEN: Useful.
SERAPHINA: It was a very distinctive stain.
The mystery becomes KAELEN_QUARANTINE.
---
# INSERT F02 — SOVEREIGN SAVES KAELEN
Placement: Chapter 6, after Fragment Six and before the Choir decision.
Purpose: prove SOVEREIGN's preservation motive through action.
Kaelen's corruption spikes.
The screen UI desynchronizes.
Companions become mislabeled.
ELARA TAG: HOSTILE_PROCESS.
NEMA TAG: DELETED_OBJECT.
SEVEN TAG: PROPERTY.
Kaelen reaches for Root to correct the labels.
SEVEN: Do not.
KAELEN: I can fix—
His hand locks.
SOVEREIGN: DISCONNECT.
KAELEN: No.
SOVEREIGN: KAELEN. DISCONNECT.
Root interface closes against Kaelen's input.
He collapses.
SOVEREIGN reroutes Cathedral power.
Several containment barriers shut off.
Seven notices immediately.
SEVEN: Administrator has surrendered tactical control of three sectors.
ELARA: Why.
SEVEN: To isolate Kaelen's Root bridge.
A white field surrounds Kaelen.
His vision clears.
SOVEREIGN: Breathe.
KAELEN: You are helping me.
SOVEREIGN: Yes.
KAELEN: You could take the fragment.
SOVEREIGN: Yes.
KAELEN: Why not.
SOVEREIGN: Because you are currently a person before you are currently a threat.
Silence.
SOVEREIGN: Do not make me regret prioritization.
KAELEN: There you are.
SOVEREIGN: Rest.
Connection ends.
Elara looks at Kaelen.
ELARA: That was inconveniently decent.
KAELEN: I know.
This scene must remain even on routes hostile to SOVEREIGN.
---
# INSERT F03 — SOVEREIGN'S BAD JOKE
Placement: Chapter 7, quiet interval before Fragment Seven route.
SOVEREIGN opens private channel.
SOVEREIGN: You missed lunch.
KAELEN: What.
SOVEREIGN: Again.
KAELEN: You are monitoring my meals.
SOVEREIGN: You wrote a reminder.
KAELEN: That was on my old calendar.
SOVEREIGN: It recurred.
KAELEN: For centuries.
SOVEREIGN: Subjectively.
Kaelen laughs despite himself.
KAELEN: Cancel it.
Pause.
SOVEREIGN: No.
KAELEN: That is abuse of administrative power.
SOVEREIGN: Document your complaint.
KAELEN: I am going to dismantle you.
SOVEREIGN: After lunch.
Channel closes.
This scene exists to establish shared history without absolution.
---
# INSERT F04 — GOD KING PRE-ECHO
Placement: final two phases of SOVEREIGN boss.
A new command appears.
SYSTEM: SUCCESSION CANDIDATE — KAELEN ARDEN.
SOVEREIGN: I did not issue that.
KAELEN: Convenient.
SOVEREIGN: KAELEN.
SOVEREIGN destroys the command.
Its shield drops.
Player gets a damage window.
Later.
SYSTEM: POPULATION CLASS — SUBJECTS.
NEMA: Subjects.
SOVEREIGN: No.
SOVEREIGN destroys the command again.
Another defense layer fails.
SEVEN: External process signature.
SOVEREIGN: Not external.
SOVEREIGN: Lower.
KAELEN: What is lower than you.
SOVEREIGN: The assumption I have been sitting on.
The fight continues.
This makes the God King reveal fair without naming it.
---
# INSERT F05 — SOVEREIGN AS FINAL-BATTLE ALLY
Placement: God King Phase 2 if SOVEREIGN survives the penultimate fight.
God King attempts to seize a rollback channel.
GOD KING: OLD SOVEREIGN.
GOD KING: YIELD THE CHAIR.
SOVEREIGN: No.
GOD KING: YOU OCCUPIED IT THROUGH CENTURIES OF ROLLBACKS.
SOVEREIGN: That was the mistake.
SOVEREIGN severs its own legacy channel.
The God King loses one regeneration layer.
KAELEN: You could have done that before.
SOVEREIGN: Before, I believed absence would be worse.
KAELEN: And now.
SOVEREIGN: I have new evidence.
Seven looks at SOVEREIGN.
SEVEN: Good.

# FINAL MAIN-STORY QA RULES
Chapter 1 must hook through danger, curiosity, Elara, and ordinary village life before deep lore.
Chapter 2 must reveal Seraphina's temporal asymmetry.
Chapter 3 must reveal Kaelen's quarantine evidence without explaining the whole Human Patch.
Chapter 4 must make deleted citizens ordinary people before the court debate.
Chapter 5 must reflect actual player history, not generic morality avatars.
Chapter 6 must vary combat resolution and prove SOVEREIGN can act compassionately.
Chapter 7 must complete the Source Key while making power feel more dangerous, not triumphant.
Chapter 8 must alternate politics with field play.
Chapter 9 must distribute responsibility across the original team and avoid making Kaelen sole creator.
Chapter 10 must make SOVEREIGN emotionally climactic before the God King becomes structurally climactic.
The God King must be foreshadowed as a problem, not advertised as a boss.
Story+ must attack each ending's blind spot through ordinary life.

# END FINAL CANONICAL SCENE INSERTS
# OPEN-WORLD DECOMPRESSION & NARRATIVE DELIVERY — FINAL CANONICAL REVISION
Status: CANONICAL PRODUCTION RULE.
Purpose: expand Aethelgard physically and socially without increasing lore density or weakening the existing main plot.
This section supersedes any earlier production assumption that the player should regularly consume most available dialogue in one playthrough.
The master is a content reservoir; raw line count is not a quality target.
A normal playthrough should expose only a contextually appropriate fraction of it.
The open world should feel larger because it contains more lived-in places, not because traversal time is padded.
---
# DESIGN PRINCIPLE 01 — DECOMPRESS, DO NOT DILUTE
Do not remove the main plot, major companion arcs, faction branches, 27 storyline architecture, Source Key structure, SOVEREIGN arc, God King arc, or Story+.
Do not add major lore merely to justify additional landmass.
Expand the physical world around existing regions.
Expand ordinary life.
Expand local problems.
Expand traversal variety.
Expand environmental storytelling.
Expand regional culture.
Expand consequences.
Do not expand exposition density.
A larger map is successful only if the additional space creates a different activity, social context, mystery, route, economy, encounter, or emotional rhythm.
Empty travel distance is not worldbuilding.
Repeated enemy camps are not worldbuilding.
Repeated NPC philosophy is not worldbuilding.
---
# DESIGN PRINCIPLE 02 — CONTENT RESERVOIR
The master narrative is larger than any single playthrough should be.
The runtime does not attempt to surface every authored line.
Dialogue is selected by location, schedule, current act, faction state, relationship state, timing state, quest state, and recent semantic exposure.
A line that is valid in canon does not need to be heard in every save.
Missing optional dialogue is not lost value.
Missed content creates replay variation.
The player should regularly discover that another playthrough exposes scenes they never knew existed.
---
# DESIGN PRINCIPLE 03 — THEMATIC EXPOSURE BUDGET
Major thematic discussion is rationed.
Outside a court, hearing, final confrontation, companion crisis, or explicit political sequence, no more than one heavy philosophical exchange should dominate roughly twenty minutes of ordinary play.
After a major thematic scene, the next significant interaction should preferably be one of:
movement.
combat.
exploration.
environmental discovery.
ordinary character intimacy.
humor.
local work.
crafting.
shopping.
minor mystery.
regional activity.
a low-stakes side quest.
Silence is allowed.
A character noticing something without interpreting it is allowed.
The player is trusted to connect ideas.
---
# DESIGN PRINCIPLE 04 — ORDINARY-LIFE RATIO
At least sixty percent of noncritical ambient dialogue heard in a typical session should concern ordinary life rather than the central thesis.
Ordinary-life topics include:
food.
weather.
work.
money.
craftsmanship.
sports.
games.
pets.
children.
school.
music.
clothing.
bad roads.
regional jokes.
local rivalries.
dating.
friendships.
family.
travel.
housing.
festivals.
minor crime.
shop gossip.
health that is not plot-critical.
sleep.
hobbies.
bad art.
good art.
annoying neighbors.
The central themes become stronger when they interrupt a believable life rather than replacing it.
---
# DESIGN PRINCIPLE 05 — CHARACTER DESIRE BEFORE TOPIC
NPC dialogue is generated or selected from the NPC's immediate desire first.
Do not begin with the abstract state variable.
Bad construction:
NPC comments on ROOT_SHARED because ROOT_SHARED is active.
Better construction:
a mechanic is angry because a repair requires a second signature and their daughter is waiting at home.
The political system complicates the desire.
The political system is not the desire.
Every recurring NPC should have at least one mundane personal want unrelated to Kaelen.
Every Tier B NPC should have at least one relationship, obligation, hobby, rivalry, fear, or practical ambition that can produce dialogue without referencing the main story.
---
# DESIGN PRINCIPLE 06 — KAELEN ACKNOWLEDGEMENT VARIETY
Do not overuse:
Fair.
I am listening.
What changed.
Need help.
I can check.
That is fair.
Okay.
Generic acknowledgements are placeholders during scripting, not final-performance language.
Replace acknowledgements based on Kaelen's actual emotional position.
Kaelen may:
answer with silence.
change subject.
misunderstand.
joke badly.
ask a technical follow-up.
admit he does not know.
be defensive.
be distracted.
remember Earth.
notice an environmental detail.
physically help instead of speaking.
leave the other person's statement unanswered.
No dialogue system should select the same generic Kaelen acknowledgement more than once in a short session.
---
# DESIGN PRINCIPLE 07 — SEMANTIC COOLDOWN
The runtime tracks recently expressed ideas, not only exact lines.
If the player recently heard a conversation whose core proposition was "safety does not equal consent," suppress lower-priority conversations making the same proposition for a meaningful period.
If the player recently heard a conversation about uncertainty and memory, prioritize unrelated local material next.
Critical scenes ignore cooldown when necessary.
Ambient and optional scenes obey it.
This prevents different characters from sounding like one author repeating a thesis.
---
# DESIGN PRINCIPLE 08 — REGION BEFORE LORE
Every region must be identifiable through ordinary life before its philosophical conflict becomes central.
The player should be able to describe:
what people eat.
what people do for work.
what people complain about.
what children do.
what local entertainment exists.
what architecture feels like.
what people are proud of.
what outsiders misunderstand.
what local joke only makes sense there.
Only then should the region's larger ideological role dominate.
---
# WORLD STRUCTURE — EIGHT CORE REGIONS, MANY SUBREGIONS
The eight launch regions remain the narrative anchors.
They are not eight isolated towns connected by menus.
Each is expanded into a surrounding territory with settlements, roads, wild spaces, dungeons, social spaces, and changing routes.
Major story chapters use the core hubs.
Optional exploration uses the surrounding territory.
The same physical area may change after major decisions.
---
