# OPEN-WORLD SCALE RULE
The eight core regions plus their surrounding subregions are sufficient for the launch game.
Do not add a ninth major kingdom merely to make the map look larger.
Add a new major region only when it introduces:
a genuinely new culture.
a new traversal identity.
a new economy.
a new conflict.
a new gameplay system.
or a story function impossible to express in existing space.
Expansion should first deepen and connect the eight existing territories.
---
# WORLD CONNECTION RULES
Regions are connected by traversable roads, gates, ferries, tunnels, storm routes, and system passages.
Fast travel exists after discovery.
The player can physically travel when desired.
Backtracking must reveal change.
Returning to a region after a major choice should show at least one visible alteration.
Examples:
new NPC schedule.
closed shop.
new shop.
bridge repair.
refugee camp.
new memorial.
different guard placement.
changed prices.
new dialogue.
new route.
new environmental hazard.
new festival.
new public notice.
Open-world return visits should never feel like walking through a frozen chapter set.
---
# SIDE-QUEST FLOW RULE
Side quests have five functional classes.
Class A — Character.
Deepens a companion or recurring NPC.
Class B — Regional.
Changes local services, routes, prices, schedules, or civic state.
Class C — Political.
Changes faction evidence, support, or policy.
Class D — Secret.
Advances hidden storyline prerequisites.
Class E — Ordinary.
Exists primarily for fun, culture, exploration, humor, craft, or everyday life.
The game needs all five.
Not every side quest should secretly feed the ending.
---
# SIDE-QUEST UNLOCK AND REMOVAL RULE
Different choices may unlock, transform, postpone, or remove side quests.
This is desirable.
It must be legible.
A side quest may disappear because:
an NPC left.
an NPC died.
an NPC was restored.
an NPC chose dormancy.
a region became inaccessible.
a service changed.
a faction solved the problem differently.
a deadline passed.
the underlying problem no longer exists.
When a quest disappears for a meaningful state reason, the world should show what happened.
Do not silently delete the quest marker with no explanation.
A closed quest may be replaced by a consequence quest.
Example:
player fails to save a caravan.
The original escort quest closes.
Later a shortage quest appears in the settlement that never received the cargo.
This makes missing content feel like story flow rather than punishment.
---
# SIDE-QUEST MUTUAL EXCLUSIVITY
Some side quests should be mutually exclusive.
Do not attempt to let one playthrough see every quest.
Examples:
a black-market investigation exists only if the player previously tolerated scarcity exploitation.
a refugee integration quest exists only if the relevant settlement accepts refugees.
an Archive privacy scandal exists only if public-record policy was expanded.
a Root-abuse investigation exists only if Kaelen used unilateral authority in the relevant case.
a release memorial quest exists only if a specific person chose release.
a restoration identity dispute exists only if multiple versions were restored.
Mutual exclusivity increases replayability.
---
# SIDE-QUEST CONSEQUENCE TIERS
Tier 1 consequence: dialogue or cosmetic.
Tier 2 consequence: NPC schedule, price, service, route, or local relationship.
Tier 3 consequence: regional state or faction support.
Tier 4 consequence: companion arc, main-story evidence, boss support, political vote, or secret-route prerequisite.
Tier 5 consequence: changes the available form of a major story decision.
Only a minority of side quests should be Tier 4 or Tier 5.
If every side quest changes the ending, the world feels artificially centered on Kaelen.
---
# DISCOVERY REWARD RULE
Exploration must reward curiosity with one or more of:
mechanical advantage.
shortcut.
rare material.
new traversal option.
character scene.
regional story.
mystery evidence.
visual spectacle.
humor.
useful map information.
secret quest.
world-state understanding.
Discovery should not repeatedly reward the player with another long lore paragraph.
Environmental stories should often be interpretable without a text log.
---
# MYSTERY DELIVERY RULE
Mystery evidence is distributed across:
main story.
optional archives.
environment.
NPC memory.
companion observations.
boss mechanics.
world geometry.
economy.
timing anomalies.
repeated symbols.
No critical first-playthrough answer should require reading every optional document.
Optional exploration should deepen or recontextualize answers.
It should not rescue an incoherent main plot.
---
# DIALOGUE SCHEDULER
Every optional dialogue candidate receives:
priority.
topic family.
emotional intensity.
speaker.
region.
cooldown.
world-state prerequisites.
relationship prerequisites.
repeatability flag.
recent-semantic similarity value.
The scheduler should prefer:
unheard character-specific material.
current local stakes.
ordinary-life material after heavy scenes.
lines that respond to recent player action.
lines that reveal new information.
The scheduler should suppress:
near-duplicate thematic statements.
generic acknowledgements used recently.
lines inconsistent with NPC schedule.
dialogue that repeats information the player just learned.
high-intensity philosophical material immediately after another high-intensity scene.
---
# DIALOGUE SILENCE RULE
A reaction does not always require dialogue.
Possible reaction outputs:
look.
pause.
animation.
walking away.
handing over an object.
changing a schedule.
changing shop price.
closing a door.
joining a task.
refusing eye contact.
sitting beside someone.
writing a note.
changing a sign.
silence.
Use silence when a spoken line would merely restate what the player already understands.
---
# REGIONAL HUMOR RULE
Each major region needs its own humor source.
Oakhaven humor: neighbors, food, weather, livestock, stubborn repair culture.
Ironhold humor: military formality, markets, arena bravado, bureaucracy.
Wastes humor: impossible geography treated as an annoying daily inconvenience.
Forgotten Sectors humor: forms, queues, absurd labels, administrative survival.
Mirror City humor: reflections, wrong identities, impossible transit, urban inconvenience.
Cathedral humor: literal systems colliding with rituals and ordinary preference.
Memory Ocean humor: people treating impossible memory geography as transport logistics.
Saved Assembly humor: meetings, minutes, committees, messages, procedural chaos.
Do not give every region the same quippy voice.
---
# REGIONAL CULTURE RULE
Every region receives:
one signature food.
one ordinary drink.
one local game.
one festival.
one children's activity.
one insult.
one compliment.
one superstition.
one local craft.
one architectural habit.
one song or musical practice.
one common job.
one local social rule outsiders can violate accidentally.
These details should enter quests and ambient life before they enter encyclopedic lore.
---
# OPEN-WORLD ENCOUNTER RULE
Do not fill larger regions with constant combat.
Traversal alternates among:
combat.
quiet travel.
NPC activity.
environmental puzzle.
resource gathering.
micro-event.
wildlife or system-creature behavior.
conversation.
weather.
discovery.
A dangerous world can still have stretches where nothing attacks the player.
That quiet makes threats more effective.
---
# DYNAMIC MICRO-EVENTS
Micro-events are short stateful events, not full quests.
Examples:
cart wheel breaks.
child loses a pet.
merchant argues over measurement.
storm changes road.
guard helps civilian.
NPCs repair a roof.
two factions share lunch.
street performer draws crowd.
minor theft.
lost letter.
broken pump.
wedding procession.
funeral crossing.
school group visiting memorial.
Seven watching sunrise.
Kaito correcting a sign.
Rook haggling and losing.
Micro-events create life without adding another quest log entry.
---
# COMPANION OPEN-WORLD PRESENCE
Companions interact with regions independently of Kaelen.
Elara helps at clinics and kitchens.
Seraphina checks exits and occasionally gets recognized by former Ironhold soldiers.
Lyra visits archives and stationery vendors.
Kaelthas argues with archivists without waiting for a quest.
Kaito walks to vantage points.
Seven investigates machinery and watches sunrise.
Nema visits ordinary shops in active districts.
Rook disappears into markets and returns with either profit or embarrassment.
These behaviors should occur without every interaction becoming a cutscene.
---
# COMPANION CONVERSATION DENSITY
Do not fire a companion conversation merely because it exists.
Camp conversation priority rises after:
a relevant major choice.
a personal quest beat.
a region tied to the companion.
a relationship-state change.
an unusual failure.
a meaningful silence.
Camp conversation priority falls after:
another long conversation.
a major hearing.
a lore-heavy dungeon.
a recent conversation with the same companion.
The player should sometimes finish a camp night with only ordinary banter.
---
# ROMANCE / INTIMACY RULE
If romance is implemented later, it is not required for companion emotional completion.
Intimacy may include:
friendship.
trust.
conflict.
shared routine.
grief.
professional respect.
chosen family.
romance.
No companion arc should become narratively incomplete because the player did not choose romance.
---
# 27 STORYLINES — ASYMMETRY RULE
The 27 storylines do not need equal scene counts.
They do not need equal quest counts.
They do not need identical post-ending structures.
They require equal narrative legitimacy, not equal mathematical shape.
One route may become:
constitutional crisis.
Another:
rescue campaign.
Another:
labor strike.
Another:
funeral and succession dispute.
Another:
first-contact negotiation.
Another:
regional reconstruction.
Another:
privacy scandal.
Another:
infrastructure emergency.
Another:
identity case.
Another:
migration crisis.
Another:
expedition.
The route's gameplay form should emerge from what that political world actually struggles with.
---
# STORY+ VARIETY RULE
Story+ is not always a political hearing.
At least half of route-defining Story+ content should occur through gameplay outside a council chamber.
Possible forms:
rescue.
escort.
investigation.
dungeon.
strike.
festival.
funeral.
reconstruction.
medical emergency.
market shock.
expedition.
court case.
public protest.
first contact.
environmental disaster.
family conflict.
Story+ should show the philosophy failing in the world before anyone explains why it failed.
---
# ROUTE DISCOVERY RULE
The player should not see the full route matrix on a first playthrough.
The game may show major commitments.
It should not show a spreadsheet of twenty-seven outcomes.
Storyline titles appear after completion.
New Game Plus may expose more structural information.
This protects surprise and prevents choices from becoming optimization.
---
# RUNTIME EXPOSURE TARGETS
These are design targets, not absolute timers.
Main-story critical dialogue remains available.
Optional heavy theme conversations should be separated by ordinary play whenever possible.
Do not surface more than a small fraction of Tier C reactions in one visit.
Do not let one NPC exhaust their entire dialogue bank because the player repeatedly presses interact.
After two or three contextually relevant lines, default to short ordinary barks until state changes.
Major companion conversations should feel discovered, not queued.
---
# OPEN-WORLD QUEST LOG RULE
The quest log should not become a census of every possible activity.
Major quests are logged.
Side quests with meaningful state are logged.
Micro-events are usually not logged.
Rumors may be tracked separately.
Discovered mysteries may enter an Evidence or Notes section rather than Quest Log.
Regional activities may appear on the map without becoming formal quests.
This reduces checklist fatigue.
---
# CONSEQUENCE PROPAGATION MODEL
Consequences propagate in layers.
Local consequence.
Regional consequence.
Faction consequence.
Companion consequence.
Main-story consequence.
Story+ consequence.
Not every choice reaches every layer.
A bridge repair may only affect trade and a later caravan.
A companion betrayal may reach the final battle.
A regional privacy law may influence Archive negotiations.
A joke choice may never matter again.
Unequal consequence weight makes the world feel natural.
---
# OPEN-WORLD ECONOMY AND STORY
Economy is part of narrative state.
Prices can react to:
caravan survival.
road access.
medicine supply.
regional stability.
worker strikes.
refugee arrivals.
restoration population.
release policy.
festival demand.
faction infrastructure.
Economic changes should be understandable from world events.
Do not turn economic systems into hidden moral scores.
Rook can explain incentives when useful.
He should not narrate every price change.
---
# OPEN-WORLD TIME
WorldClock remains.
Time-sensitive quests use visible reasons and warnings.
A larger map must not make travel time unfair.
When a deadline matters, the player receives:
distance estimate.
known route risk.
fast-travel status.
deadline explanation.
optional extension or preparation route when fiction permits.
Difficulty settings may change timing leniency without changing the story's causal logic.
---
# TRAVEL AND BACKTRACKING
Travel should support three modes.
Direct route.
Safer route.
Exploration route.
Direct is faster and riskier.
Safer is predictable.
Exploration may uncover resources, quests, scenery, shortcuts, or secrets.
No route should be objectively correct every time.
Backtracking should become faster through unlocked transport, knowledge, shortcuts, and fast travel.
The game should not waste the player's time to prove the map is large.
---
# WORLD MAP
The world map records what the player has actually learned.
Unknown routes remain incomplete.
Kaito can improve map information.
Some protected locations remain deliberately vague if residents requested privacy.
Map changes can communicate consequence.
Examples:
bridge restored.
road removed.
settlement relocated.
new refugee quarter.
quarantine lifted.
archive opened.
tram restored.
storm route changed.
Map information is narrative, not only navigation.
---
# MAJOR PLOT PROTECTION
Open-world expansion must not dilute these mandatory beats:
Kaelen's first relationship with Elara.
Seraphina and the Flight 707 time gap.
Lyra and memory uncertainty.
Kaelthas betrayal.
Null Court standing.
Mirror City self-confrontation.
Seven's self-definition.
Source Key completion.
Saved Assembly commitments.
Human Patch truth.
SOVEREIGN confrontation.
God King final authority conflict.
Expansion goes around these beats.
It does not replace or endlessly delay them.
---
# PACING PROTECTION
The player should feel a change of emotional texture between regions.
Oakhaven begins intimate and grounded.
Ironhold raises scale and pressure.
Wastes opens exploration and uncertainty.
Forgotten Sectors slows into personhood and civic life.
Mirror City becomes uncanny and personal.
Cathedral combines spectacle, care, and ideology.
Memory Ocean becomes reflective and beautiful.
Saved Assembly becomes political but mobile.
Human Patch becomes intimate and historical.
Root of Heaven becomes climactic and structural.
Open-world content should reinforce these textures rather than flattening them.
---
# THRILL AND ADVENTURE RULE
The philosophical story does not replace adventure.
Every act needs:
at least one memorable traversal set piece.
at least one dangerous optional location.
at least one boss or major encounter with a mechanical surprise.
at least one mystery reveal.
at least one character payoff.
at least one low-stakes joy scene.
at least one region visibly changed by the player.
Thrill comes from uncertainty, movement, risk, mastery, and consequence.
Not from constant combat.
---
# PLAYER AGENCY RULE
The player can leave many optional problems unresolved.
NPCs may solve problems without Kaelen.
Factions may act while the player is elsewhere.
A late arrival should sometimes reveal that the world continued.
This is a feature.
Kaelen is important.
Kaelen is not the clock the universe runs on.
---
# NPC AUTONOMY RULE
Named NPCs may:
change job.
move house.
join faction.
leave faction.
start relationship.
end relationship.
open shop.
close shop.
recover.
decline recovery.
become politically active.
retire.
fail.
succeed without Kaelen.
These changes should be constrained by authored state logic.
They should not be random personality mutation.
---
# FAILURE RULE
Failure often creates content.
Failed escort may create shortage.
Missed hearing may create appeal crisis.
Lost fight may change reputation.
Late arrival may shift leadership.
Failed rescue may create memorial and political pressure.
Do not convert every failure into reload pressure.
Some failures should be more narratively interesting than success.
---
# PLAYER KNOWLEDGE VS CHARACTER KNOWLEDGE
The open world may allow the player to discover clues Kaelen does not immediately understand.
The UI should distinguish:
observed fact.
Kaelen's interpretation.
companion interpretation.
unverified rumor.
archival claim.
system label.
This supports mystery without pretending uncertain information is fact.
---
# LORE TEXT LIMIT
Optional readable logs should usually be short.
Long archival documents are rare and deliberately valuable.
Critical lore should be dramatized or summarized through interaction.
A large world should not become a library of walls of text.
---
# ENVIRONMENTAL STORY RULE
A room should be able to tell a story through:
object placement.
damage.
repair.
missing objects.
repeated objects.
signage.
schedule.
lighting.
architecture.
music.
NPC behavior.
price.
route access.
A text log is optional reinforcement.
---
# REPLAYABILITY RULE
Replayability comes from:
different faction path.
different Root authority.
different deleted-person policy.
different companion relationships.
different timing.
different region outcomes.
different side-quest availability.
different secret prerequisites.
different discovery order.
different Story+ crisis.
It should not depend on replaying an identical first thirty hours to reach one late choice.
New Game Plus may accelerate previously mastered mandatory segments.
---
# NEW GAME PLUS OPEN-WORLD RULE
New Game Plus may:
unlock alternate starting information.
surface the long Flight 707 prologue.
accelerate tutorials.
allow earlier route awareness.
add remixed enemy behavior.
open previously inaccessible exploration pockets.
preserve cosmetic collections.
add meta-memory conversations where appropriate.
It must not invalidate the first playthrough.
---
# IMPLEMENTATION PRIORITY
Phase OW-1.
Build traversal and physical connections among the eight core regions.
Phase OW-2.
Add schedules and ordinary-life activity to core hubs.
Phase OW-3.
Add two or three high-value subregions per core region.
Phase OW-4.
Add consequence-based world changes.
Phase OW-5.
Add remaining subregions selectively based on gameplay value.
Phase OW-6.
Add semantic dialogue cooldown and state-aware delivery.
Phase OW-7.
Add side-quest mutual exclusivity and consequence replacements.
Phase OW-8.
Add route-specific Story+ asymmetry.
Phase OW-9.
Run blind pacing tests.
Do not build all eighty listed subregions before validating whether the first sixteen are fun.
The list defines world potential, not a requirement to produce empty space.
---
# BLIND PLAYTEST QUESTIONS
After each major build, ask players:
What did you think Aethelgard was after two hours.
What mystery were you most curious about.
Which companion did you trust and why.
Which region felt most alive.
Which region felt like a level rather than a place.
Did any character sound like another character.
Did the game repeat an idea you already understood.
Which side quest felt consequential.
Which side quest felt like filler.
Did you ever discover a consequence you did not expect.
Did you ever feel punished for exploring.
Did you ever feel rushed without understanding why.
Did you ever feel the world waited unrealistically for you.
Which ordinary moment do you remember.
Which boss felt connected to the story.
Which choice made you stop and think.
Which choice felt fake.
What did you predict correctly.
What surprised you fairly.
What confused you for the wrong reason.
Would you replay to see another route.
---
# OPEN-WORLD FINAL QA
The world may grow larger.
The critical path must not become more diluted.
The dialogue database may remain enormous.
The player's actual dialogue exposure must remain curated.
The map may contain more places.
Every place needs a gameplay, social, emotional, economic, exploratory, or narrative reason to exist.
The story remains about people living under systems.
The game also remains about traveling, fighting, laughing, eating, exploring, failing, finding things, and going home.
Aethelgard should feel worth saving before the player is asked how to save it.
---
# END OPEN-WORLD DECOMPRESSION & NARRATIVE DELIVERY REVISION
# FINAL GAME-SYSTEMS AUDIT & ENHANCEMENT CONTRACT
Status: CANONICAL SYSTEMS PLAN.
Purpose: define which systems Aethelgard requires, which existing systems need refinement, and which tempting systems are explicitly rejected because they would add friction, dilute the narrative, or multiply production risk.
This section distinguishes narrative-state systems already strong in the master from RPG systems that were previously only implied.
---
# SYSTEM STATUS LEGEND
KEEP = already strong and should remain.
REFINE = already present but needs explicit mechanical rules.
ADD = materially improves the game and is not sufficiently specified yet.
OPTIONAL = valuable only if implementation quality and schedule allow.
REJECT = do not add to the launch design unless the game changes fundamentally.
---
# 01 — PLAYER CHOICE / CONSEQUENCE
Status: KEEP.
The existing 27-storyline architecture remains.
Choices affect scenes, regions, factions, companions, timing, bosses, side quests, economy, and Story+.
Choices are not reduced to ending selection.
Major choices must change later behavior or world state.
Minor choices may remain emotional, cosmetic, local, humorous, or relational.
No choice is required to affect every system.
---
# 02 — COMPANION SYSTEM
Status: KEEP + REFINE MECHANICALLY.
Eight major companions remain.
Trust, Respect, and Reliance remain separate.
Trust: does the companion believe Kaelen tells the truth.
Respect: does the companion believe Kaelen listens.
Reliance: how practically or emotionally dependent the companion has become on Kaelen.
High Reliance is not automatically positive.
No single approval meter replaces this model.
---
# COMPANION FIELD RULE
General open-world exploration supports one primary active combat companion at a time.
Story encounters may temporarily use more than one companion when authored for it.
This prevents eight-character combat clutter and allows each companion AI to remain readable.
Companion swapping occurs at camps, safe hubs, or other clear authored points.
Emergency story swaps may occur when fiction requires them.
---
# COMPANION COMBAT COMMANDS
Use a small command set rather than tactical micromanagement.
Suggested commands:
Focus Target.
Protect.
Hold Position.
Use Signature.
Regroup.
Companions otherwise act autonomously according to combat identity.
The player should not manage companion inventory every ten seconds.
---
# COMPANION SYNERGY
Trust/Respect/Reliance may unlock:
new conversation.
new assist behavior.
new combination technique.
new rescue behavior.
new tactical option.
new field interaction.
They should not simply grant generic +10 percent friendship damage.
Political disagreement can coexist with excellent combat coordination.
---
# COMPANION PROGRESSION
Each companion receives a compact authored progression track.
Prefer two or three meaningful branches over a giant skill tree.
Branches reflect fighting style and character history.
Companion gear should use curated signature equipment plus a small number of upgrades.
Do not create a second full loot-management game for all eight companions.
---
# 03 — COMBAT CORE
Status: REFINE + ADD FORMAL SPECIFICATION.
The master already contains dodge, parry, counters, Root interaction, stagger-like boss states, and character-specific combat identities.
The combat system now requires a formal player-facing ruleset.
---
# COMBAT RESOURCE — STAMINA
Add Stamina.
Stamina governs:
dodge.
heavy attacks.
guard pressure.
selected mobility skills.
selected weapon techniques.
Normal basic attacks should not make the game feel constantly exhausted.
Stamina regeneration begins quickly after commitment windows.
The purpose is rhythm and decision-making, not waiting.
---
# EQUIPMENT LOAD
Add equipment load.
Use three readable movement classes:
Light.
Medium.
Heavy.
Load primarily comes from equipped weapon, shield, armor, and selected heavy tools.
Do not make every crafting material add annoying carry weight.
Light favors movement and recovery.
Medium is balanced.
Heavy favors guard, stability, and impact.
No class should become an obvious best choice.
---
# DODGE
Formalize dodge invulnerability frames.
Invulnerability is consistent and learnable.
Visual feedback must communicate successful avoidance.
Difficulty/accessibility settings may widen timing without changing story state.
Dodge distance and recovery may vary by load class.
---
# PARRY / PERFECT GUARD
Formalize parry.
Parry windows depend more on player skill than hidden stats.
Successful parry may:
stagger.
reduce posture.
open counter.
interrupt selected attacks.
Not every boss attack is parryable.
Telegraphs must make this readable.
---
# SHIELD BASH / GUARD BREAK
Add or formalize shield bash and guard break.
Purpose:
interrupt selected enemies.
break defensive posture.
create space.
support shield-focused builds.
It must not replace parry, dodge, and positioning.
---
# ATTACK COMMITMENT
Formalize attack animation commitment.
Normal attacks have readable commitment and recovery.
The player cannot cancel every mistake instantly.
Selected skills and advanced mastery may gain specific cancel windows.
This prevents button-mashing without making controls feel unresponsive.
---
# POISE / STAGGER
Add a clear stagger system.
Enemies have readable stability/posture behavior.
Heavy weapons and selected skills deal greater stagger.
Boss stagger windows are authored and cannot be permanently looped.
---
# HIT FEEL
Combat quality requires:
hit pause where appropriate.
impact animation.
sound differentiation.
camera response with accessibility toggle.
enemy recoil.
clean hurtboxes.
clean attack telegraphs.
These presentation systems are part of combat quality, not optional polish.
---
# STATUS SYSTEM
Add a small curated status-effect system.
Do not add twenty nearly identical elemental bars.
Recommended categories:
Fracture.
Bleed or Wound.
Burn or Heat.
Shock or Disrupt.
Slow or Bind.
Guard Break.
Memory Distortion for selected system enemies.
Corruption remains separate from normal status effects because it is also narrative.
---
# ROOT COMBAT
Root abilities remain powerful but bounded.
Root actions can manipulate:
enemy directive.
arena object.
hazard.
process state.
selected status.
selected defense.
Root cannot become a universal instant-win spell.
Root corruption increases through aggressive use.
Root corruption has clear UI and recovery methods.
---
# 04 — PLAYER PROGRESSION
Status: ADD.
The current master lacks a complete XP / level / skill-tree specification.
---
# LEVELING
Use experience from:
combat.
bosses.
quests.
exploration discoveries.
major civic resolutions.
Do not reward only killing.
Exploration and noncombat play must remain viable.
Avoid infinite exponential stat inflation.
Late levels should improve build expression more than simply doubling damage.
---
# PLAYER ATTRIBUTES
Keep the attribute list small.
Recommended foundation:
Vitality — health and survival.
Endurance — stamina and load.
Might — heavy physical scaling and stagger.
Finesse — fast weapon scaling and precision.
Focus — Root control and technical skills.
Resolve — corruption resistance, recovery, selected defensive effects.
Exact names may change to fit world language.
Do not create fifteen attributes.
---
# SKILL FAMILIES
Add compact player skill trees or skill webs.
Recommended families:
Bladecraft.
Guard.
Mobility.
Root.
Fracture.
Survival / Fieldcraft.
Craft / Tools may exist as a support progression track rather than combat tree.
Trees should unlock new behavior, not mostly +2 percent bonuses.
---
# RESPEC
Add accessible respec after the early game.
Respec should cost something meaningful but not permanently punish experimentation.
Story choices are not respec-able.
Build choices are.
---
# REGION LEVELING
Use soft regional difficulty bands plus dangerous pockets.
Do not scale every enemy exactly to the player's level.
Earlier regions may gain high-level optional variants or Story+ threats.
Backtracking should feel empowering while still containing new danger.
---
# 05 — WEAPON SYSTEM
Status: ADD.
Weapons currently exist narratively but not as a complete mechanical taxonomy.
Recommended core weapon families:
Longsword.
Greatblade.
Twin Blades.
Spear.
Hammer.
Dagger.
Arc Blade or magical hybrid.
Root Gauntlet / system tool.
Bow or equivalent ranged weapon if ranged combat quality is strong enough.
Shield as off-hand / build-defining equipment.
Final weapon count may be smaller if animation quality would suffer.
Quality of movesets is more important than number of categories.
---
# WEAPON IDENTITY
Each weapon family needs:
distinct basic chain.
heavy attack.
running attack.
air attack if aerial combat exists.
dodge attack.
charged option where appropriate.
signature skill slot.
stagger profile.
range and recovery identity.
Do not create ten weapon skins with identical moves.
---
# WEAPON MASTERY
Using a weapon family may unlock mastery nodes.
Mastery should unlock:
new move.
counter option.
alternate finisher.
utility.
stance.
not endless flat damage grinding.
Mastery should have a reasonable cap.
---
# EQUIPMENT RARITY
Use a restrained rarity system.
Suggested:
Common.
Refined.
Rare.
Relic.
Unique.
Named equipment may ignore normal rarity.
Avoid randomized affix explosions.
A player should remember important equipment by identity, not by a spreadsheet of +3.7 percent modifiers.
---
# UNIQUE / BOSS EQUIPMENT
Bosses and major quest lines may grant unique weapons, armor, charms, techniques, or crafting cores.
Named equipment should connect mechanically and narratively to its source.
Do not require extreme low-probability boss farming for core builds.
---
# NO WEAPON DURABILITY
Status: REJECT.
Routine weapon durability would add maintenance friction without strengthening Aethelgard's core play.
Repair may exist for story or crafting events.
Player weapons should not constantly break through ordinary use.
---
# 06 — ARMOR / ACCESSORIES
Status: ADD.
Armor influences:
defense.
equipment load.
selected resistances.
poise/stability.
possibly one meaningful passive.
Avoid full armor sets where the only difference is tiny numerical variation.
Accessories / charms provide build modifiers.
Keep accessory slots limited enough that choices remain readable.
---
# 07 — ITEM / INVENTORY SYSTEM
Status: ADD.
Item categories:
Consumables.
Crafting materials.
Weapons.
Armor.
Accessories.
Combat tools.
Quest items.
Lore/evidence objects.
Trade goods.
Relics / Root artifacts.
---
# INVENTORY FRICTION RULE
Do not use survival-style inventory Tetris.
Common materials may stack generously.
Quest items never consume frustrating capacity.
Equipment load affects what is worn, not the player's ability to carry herbs.
A stash is available at camps/hubs.
Critical loot should not be lost because inventory was full.
---
# QUICK ITEMS
Combat quick slots remain limited and intentional.
The player may reconfigure them outside immediate danger.
Consumable use has animation commitment so items are not free healing during unsafe moments.
---
# 08 — CRAFTING
Status: ADD.
Crafting currently exists only as environmental references.
Add focused crafting, not a factory simulator.
Craft categories:
healing / stabilizers.
combat consumables.
weapon enhancement.
armor enhancement.
utility tools.
regional specialty items.
selected Root components.
---
# CRAFTING IDENTITY
Different regions contribute different materials and methods.
Oakhaven: herbal / agricultural.
Ironhold: smithing / industrial.
Wastes: salvage / anomaly materials.
Forgotten Sectors: restoration / memory components.
Mirror City: glass / provenance / projection materials.
Cathedral: system components / medical tools.
Memory Ocean: archive materials / recovered relics.
Saved Assembly: cross-region advanced recipes.
---
# RECIPE DISCOVERY
Recipes may come from:
teachers.
side quests.
experimentation.
books.
boss cores.
regional reputation.
Do not make essential healing dependent on a missable secret recipe.
---
# 09 — ENEMY ECOLOGY / FARMING / GRINDING
Status: ADD.
The master contains enemies, bosses, hunts, and optional bosses but lacks a full farmable-enemy system.
Each major region should have roughly six to ten normal enemy families including variants.
Exact counts may be lower if animation quality would suffer.
---
# ENEMY TIERS
Common.
Veteran.
Elite.
Rare.
Field Boss / Mini-boss.
Story Boss.
Optional Superboss.
Named story bosses do not casually respawn.
Normal enemies respawn according to rest/travel/world-state rules.
---
# FARMING REWARDS
Farmable enemies can provide:
XP.
currency.
regional materials.
crafting components.
weapon mastery.
rare but reasonable drops.
Do not build important progression around 0.1 percent drop rates.
Rare items may have deterministic alternatives such as bounty completion, crafting, or pity thresholds.
---
# FARMING ROUTES
Each region can contain natural farming routes for different goals:
XP.
currency.
smithing material.
herbs.
Root component.
rare enemy.
No route is mandatory.
Grinding lets underprepared players strengthen themselves before difficult content.
Skilled players can progress with less grinding.
---
# ENEMY WORLD-STATE CHANGE
Enemy populations can change after story actions.
Examples:
destroying a Fracture source reduces one enemy type.
opening a trade road attracts bandits.
restoring a region creates new maintenance enemies.
Story+ produces altered variants.
This makes combat part of world consequence.
---
# BOUNTY / HUNT SYSTEM
Status: ADD, lightweight.
Named elites and dangerous creatures may appear through regional hunt boards or rumors.
Hunts provide:
unique materials.
named gear.
regional reputation.
optional challenge.
Do not turn the game into an endless generic bounty board.
Every named hunt should have at least one distinctive behavior, location, or story detail.
---
# OPTIONAL SUPERBOSSES
Status: ADD.
A small number of optional superbosses should exceed critical-path difficulty.
They may test:
parry mastery.
mobility.
Root restraint.
companion synergy.
status management.
build adaptation.
They should reward unique gear, lore, cosmetics, or mastery.
Do not make them required for the main ending.
---
# 10 — SHOP / MARKET / ECONOMY
Status: KEEP + FORMALIZE.
The master already contains dynamic prices, auctions, market scarcity, regional trade, opening/closing shops, economic consequences, and Rook's market role.
---
# MAIN CURRENCY
Use one primary everyday currency for readability.
Regional trade goods and special tokens may exist.
Avoid five or six mandatory currencies for ordinary purchases.
Special currencies must have a clear purpose.
---
# SHOP ARCHETYPES
Oakhaven:
herbalist.
smith.
general goods.
bakery / food.
regional craft.
Ironhold:
weapon smith.
armor smith.
combat specialist.
auction.
industrial market.
Wastes:
salvage exchange.
map / exploration trader.
storm-material trader.
Forgotten Sectors:
restoration supplies.
legal / memory trade.
ordinary civic market.
Mirror City:
projection / provenance goods.
cosmetics.
anomaly equipment.
Cathedral:
medical supply.
system components.
repair tools.
Memory Ocean:
archive relics.
reconstruction materials.
Saved Assembly:
cross-region exchange.
faction vendors.
late-game specialist.
---
# DYNAMIC PRICE RULE
Prices respond to major understandable events.
Do not simulate every onion in real time.
Dynamic pricing focuses on categories affected by:
supply route.
war / siege.
medicine shortage.
strike.
festival.
refugee arrival.
restoration population.
infrastructure.
weather.
Player choices can create opportunities and shortages.
Buy/sell spreads and transport costs prevent trivial infinite arbitrage.
---
# AUCTIONS
Status: KEEP, optional.
Auctions remain optional side content.
No main-story progression requires gambling.
Auction manipulation can create story consequences.
---
# BLACK MARKET
Status: CONDITIONAL ADD.
A black market appears only when world conditions create one.
Scarcity, prohibition, or faction policy may enable it.
It is not permanently present in every region.
Rook can interact with it.
---
# 11 — REPUTATION / CONDUCT / CRIME
Status: ADD FORMAL SYSTEM.
Do not add Good/Evil.
Do not add Righteous/Evil.
Do not use red-versus-blue karma.
---
# REGIONAL REPUTATION
Track reputation by major region.
Reputation changes:
merchant treatment.
rumors.
minor quest availability.
prices in selected cases.
guards.
NPC willingness to help.
It does not replace authored relationships.
---
# FACTION STANDING
Track standing with:
Hearth.
Archive.
Continuity.
Standing influences access and support.
Final faction choice is still a story decision, not simply whichever bar is highest.
---
# CONDUCT PROFILE
Track behavioral tendencies internally.
Suggested dimensions:
Transparent ↔ Secretive.
Interventionist ↔ Hands-Off.
Forgiving ↔ Retributive.
Collective ↔ Individual.
Risk-Tolerant ↔ Safety-Oriented.
Procedural ↔ Improvisational.
These are descriptors, not moral scores.
They may alter dialogue, reputation, available arguments, and companion interpretation.
They do not label the player good or evil.
---
# CRIME / WANTED
Status: CONDITIONAL.
Only build a full crime system if the game actually allows meaningful theft, civilian assault, illegal entry, fraud, or smuggling.
If those actions are supported, track:
witnessed crime.
local suspicion.
bounty / fine.
guard response.
merchant blacklist.
legal appeal.
Different regions may define offenses differently.
Do not create a crime system just to imitate other open-world RPGs.
---
# 12 — QUEST / JOURNAL / EVIDENCE
Status: REFINE.
The master already has quest logs and Evidence/Notes concepts.
Add a formal player-facing information architecture.
---
# JOURNAL TABS
Recommended:
Main.
Side.
Completed.
Closed / Changed.
Evidence.
People.
Regions.
Bestiary.
Tutorial / Help.
Closed quests show why they closed when the player reasonably knows the reason.
Do not shame players for mutually exclusive content.
---
# EVIDENCE SYSTEM
The Evidence section distinguishes:
Observed Fact.
System Label.
Archive Claim.
NPC Testimony.
Rumor.
Kaelen Interpretation.
Companion Interpretation.
Unresolved.
This supports mystery without making unreliable information look objective.
---
# BESTIARY
Status: ADD.
Bestiary entries unlock through encounters, observation, NPC knowledge, and hunts.
Entries can show:
behavior.
known weaknesses.
regional habitat.
drops.
lore where appropriate.
Do not reveal hidden boss mechanics before discovery.
---
# CODEX
Status: ADD, lightweight.
Use concise entries.
Do not turn the game into a second encyclopedia.
Critical understanding must remain in play.
---
# 13 — WORLD MAP / FAST TRAVEL
Status: KEEP + REFINE.
The master already defines learned map information, Kaito influence, changing routes, privacy-protected locations, and fast travel after discovery.
---
# MAP LAYERS
Recommended layers:
regions.
settlements.
routes.
fast travel.
quest markers.
rumors.
resources the player has discovered.
danger / hunt areas.
player notes if practical.
Do not mark every secret automatically.
---
# FAST TRAVEL
Unlock locations through discovery.
Fast travel should respect major active danger when fiction requires it.
Do not use long runbacks to punish boss retries.
Physical travel remains valuable because events and discoveries occur on routes.
---
# 14 — WORLD TIME / DAY-NIGHT / WEATHER
Status: WorldClock KEEP; day/night ADD LIGHTWEIGHT.
The master already has WorldClock, deadlines, seasons, weather, tides, storms, and schedules.
Add a readable day/night cycle if technically practical.
---
# DAY / NIGHT RULE
Time affects:
NPC schedules.
shop hours.
selected enemies.
selected secrets.
lighting.
some quests.
Do not force players to stand idle waiting.
Allow time-skip at camps, inns, or safe locations.
Critical quests clearly display timing.
---
# WEATHER
Status: KEEP + FORMALIZE.
Weather affects selected:
visibility.
routes.
enemy behavior.
resources.
ambient dialogue.
events.
Do not let random weather silently fail major quests.
Story-critical weather is authored or clearly forecast.
---
# SEASONS
Status: STORY-STATE, NOT REAL-TIME SIMULATION.
Seasons may change through chapter/world-state progression.
Do not require players to wait real hours or days for seasons.
---
# 15 — SAVE / LOAD / DEFEAT / RETRY
Status: ADD FORMAL SYSTEM.
The master currently preserves WorldClock state but does not define the overall save architecture.
---
# SAVE STRUCTURE
Multiple manual save slots.
Rolling autosaves.
Autosave before major irreversible story locks.
Autosave after major boss victory.
Autosave at safe hub / travel transitions where appropriate.
Do not overwrite the player's only recoverable pre-choice save.
---
# SAVE DATA
Persist:
world state.
WorldClock.
quest states.
closed-quest reasons.
NPC state.
companion Trust / Respect / Reliance.
faction standing.
regional reputation.
economy state.
map state.
enemy world-state flags.
inventory / progression.
Story+ route.
---
# SAVE MIGRATION
Because the project is long-term, saves need versioning and migration support.
Do not assume save schema will never change.
Major updates should preserve valid old saves when feasible.
---
# DEFEAT
Routine combat defeat is primarily gameplay retry abstraction.
Do not imply that every player death canonically caused a full continuity restoration.
Narrative deaths and restorations occur only when explicitly authored.
---
# RETRY
Boss retry point should be close to the arena.
No long repetitive corpse run.
Selected resources may reset according to combat balance.
The game should test the boss, not the player's tolerance for walking.
---
# 16 — CAMP / HOME BASE
Status: REFINE.
The master already has camp conversations and faction-dependent Story+ home bases.
Add a lightweight functional camp / base system.
---
# CAMP FUNCTIONS
rest.
time skip.
companion swap.
stash.
crafting.
loadout.
selected conversations.
meal / temporary preparation buff if desired.
quest planning.
Do not turn camp into a mandatory management simulator.
---
# HOME BASE
The home base may visually evolve with story and faction state.
Light decoration and trophies are optional.
Do not build a massive construction/base-building game.
---
# 17 — EXPLORATION / DUNGEONS / SECRETS
Status: KEEP + REFINE.
The expanded world includes dungeons, environmental puzzles, optional bosses, changing routes, and dangerous areas.
---
# ABILITY-GATED BACKTRACKING
Use a limited number of meaningful traversal unlocks.
Examples:
grapple.
phase step.
Root relay.
hazard protection.
map decode.
companion-specific access.
These create rewarding return visits.
Do not lock half the world behind arbitrary colored keys.
---
# SECRET AREAS
Status: ADD EXPLICITLY.
Secret areas may contain:
unique gear.
rare materials.
character scenes.
mystery evidence.
superboss.
shortcut.
visual reward.
Not every secret contains lore.
---
# PUZZLES
Status: KEEP + EXPAND SELECTIVELY.
Use environment and world rules.
Avoid constant slider/lock puzzles disconnected from setting.
Puzzle hints can be adjusted independently through accessibility options.
---
# 18 — DIFFICULTY
Status: REFINE.
The master references normal and Hell difficulty but lacks a complete difficulty contract.
Difficulty should change challenge, not narrative legitimacy.
---
# DIFFICULTY SETTINGS
Recommended:
Story.
Standard.
Veteran.
Hell.
Custom Assist.
Story does not remove consequences.
Hell does not unlock the "real" ending.
---
# CUSTOM ASSIST
Independent options may include:
incoming damage.
enemy aggression.
parry window.
dodge window.
stamina cost.
boss checkpoint behavior.
timed-quest leniency.
puzzle hints.
navigation assistance.
None should alter route validity unless the user explicitly chooses a narrative-changing option.
---
# 19 — ACCESSIBILITY
Status: ADD FULL SPECIFICATION.
Current master has only isolated accessibility safeguards.
Minimum support:
full input remapping.
controller support.
keyboard/mouse support.
text size.
dialogue speed.
subtitle speaker labels.
high-contrast UI option.
color-independent telegraphs.
screen shake slider / off.
flash reduction.
motion / camera sensitivity options.
hold/toggle choices.
QTE simplification if QTEs exist.
audio channel controls.
combat timing assists.
navigation aids.
Accessibility does not reduce achievements or story access.
---
# 20 — UI / HUD
Status: ADD FORMAL SPECIFICATION.
Combat HUD should show only actionable information.
Core combat elements:
health.
stamina.
Root corruption.
quick items.
weapon / stance.
active companion status.
important boss state when relevant.
Do not fill the screen with faction or morality meters during combat.
---
# WORLD UI
Map.
Quest / journal.
Evidence.
Inventory.
Equipment.
Skills.
Companions.
Reputation / faction status.
Bestiary / codex.
Settings.
Story route axes should remain partially hidden until narratively committed.
---
# 21 — TUTORIAL / ONBOARDING
Status: REFINE.
Teach systems through play where possible.
Aldric tutorial teaches combat fundamentals.
Ironhold arena can provide optional practice.
Market tutorial teaches economy.
Training spaces allow players to test weapons and respecs without cost.
Do not front-load twenty tutorial popups.
Previously learned tutorials can be reviewed in Help.
NG+ can skip or accelerate basic tutorials.
---
# 22 — AUDIO / MUSIC
Status: ADD AS PRODUCTION LAYER.
Adaptive regional music enhances exploration and route consequence.
Music can react to:
region.
combat.
boss phase.
major world state.
Story+.
Do not change every decision with a dramatic sting.
Silence remains useful.
Important combat telegraphs should also have audio cues.
Accessibility requires separate music/effects/dialogue controls.
---
# 23 — LOCALIZATION READINESS
Status: ADD AS PRODUCTION REQUIREMENT.
The enormous dialogue system must use stable dialogue IDs.
Do not hard-code logic to English wording.
UI must support text expansion.
Speaker labels and variables must be localization-safe.
Line concatenation should be avoided for important dialogue because grammar differs across languages.
Localization readiness is cheaper when built early.
---
# 24 — NARRATIVE / STATE DEBUGGING
Status: ADD AS DEVELOPMENT REQUIREMENT.
A 27-route stateful RPG requires internal debug tools.
Developer state inspector should display:
story axis.
quest flags.
WorldClock.
companion relationships.
reputation.
faction standing.
economy flags.
NPC locations.
secret prerequisites.
ending eligibility.
---
# AUTOMATED STORY TESTS
Add automated validation for:
all 24 standard route combinations.
all 3 secret routes.
invalid route interception.
quest mutual exclusions.
closed-content reasons.
timing states.
companion departure / return states.
save/load determinism.
Story+ entry.
No dead-end state should require manual discovery alone.
---
# CONTENT MODULARIZATION
Status: ADD AS PRODUCTION REQUIREMENT.
The narrative master remains the canonical source.
Implementation should split content into modules:
Core Lore Bible.
Critical Path.
Companion Bible.
Quest Database.
Dialogue Database.
Route / Ending Matrix.
Systems Bible.
Enemy / Boss Database.
Item / Economy Database.
World / Region Database.
Story+.
QA / Validation.
This reduces contradiction risk without deleting content.
---
# 25 — ACHIEVEMENTS / COMPLETION
Status: OPTIONAL, LIGHTWEIGHT.
Achievements may reward:
discovery.
challenge.
unusual choices.
companion arcs.
optional bosses.
exploration.
Do not award an achievement that calls one political ending the correct ending.
Do not pressure players to violate role-play simply for completion unless clearly optional.
---
# 26 — REGION-SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES / MINI-GAMES
Status: KEEP AS SMALL ACTIVITIES, NOT A GIANT SYSTEM.
Fishing may exist where it fits.
Arena exhibitions.
village games.
map surveying.
auctions.
crafting contests.
tram challenges.
choir performances.
ferry work.
regional festivals.
Each activity should reinforce region identity.
Do not add twenty shallow mini-games simply to advertise content count.
---
# 27 — ROMANCE
Status: OPTIONAL.
Romance can enhance selected companion relationships if written at the quality of the main cast.
It is not required for launch.
It never replaces friendship or ideological conflict.
No companion's emotional arc becomes incomplete without romance.
---
# 28 — SYSTEMS EXPLICITLY REJECTED FOR LAUNCH
Binary Good/Evil or Righteous/Evil meter.
Universal enemy level scaling.
Randomized gear-affix explosion.
Routine weapon durability.
Mandatory hunger/thirst survival simulation.
Massive freeform base-building.
Mandatory crafting grind.
Forced multiplayer or co-op.
Procedurally generated main quests.
Procedurally generated replacement for authored world regions.
Daily-login/live-service mechanics.
Multiple ordinary currencies with no clear purpose.
Extremely low-probability required drops.
Long boss runbacks.
Punitive inventory Tetris.
Map size for its own sake.
A full stealth game layered on top of combat unless later prototypes prove it excellent.
A mount system added only because other open worlds have mounts.
---
# 29 — CONDITIONAL SYSTEMS
Crime/Wanted: only if meaningful illegal player actions exist.
Stealth: only for authored infiltration or later prototype; no full systemic stealth at launch by default.
Mounts/Vehicles: only if expanded travel scale proves walking/transit/fast travel insufficient.
Housing decoration: only as light personalization after core systems are complete.
Photo Mode: useful polish if camera architecture supports it cleanly.
Voice Acting: production decision; the written story must work without assuming full voice coverage.
---
# 30 — FINAL PRIORITY ORDER
P0 — REQUIRED FOR CORE GAME QUALITY
Combat formalization.
Save/load/retry.
Player progression.
Weapon/item/equipment.
Enemy ecology/farming.
Quest/state persistence.
Companion combat behavior.
UI/HUD.
Accessibility.
Map/fast travel.
P1 — REQUIRED FOR RPG DEPTH
Crafting.
economy/shop formalization.
regional/faction reputation.
conduct profile.
journal/evidence/bestiary.
day/night scheduling.
weather mechanics.
camp/home-base functions.
secret areas / optional bosses.
P2 — HIGH-VALUE POLISH / REPLAYABILITY
adaptive audio.
regional mini-activities.
achievements.
light home-base personalization.
additional superbosses.
expanded Story+ content.
optional romance.
P3 — ONLY IF PROTOTYPE PROVES VALUE
crime/wanted.
expanded stealth.
mounts/vehicles.
photo mode.
full voice acting.
---
# FINAL SYSTEMS PRINCIPLE
Every system must earn its place by improving at least one of:
combat expression.
exploration.
player agency.
world reactivity.
character attachment.
build diversity.
pacing.
clarity.
replayability.
immersion.
If a system mainly creates chores, menu time, duplicated content, or implementation risk without improving those goals, cut the system.
Aethelgard should be deep because systems interact.
It should not be deep because it contains the largest number of systems.
---
# END FINAL GAME-SYSTEMS AUDIT & ENHANCEMENT CONTRACT
# IMPLEMENTATION ROADMAP — DEPENDENCY-AWARE PRODUCTION PLAN
Status: CANONICAL DEVELOPMENT ORDER.
Purpose: turn the narrative/world/systems master into a buildable game without implementing high-cost content before the underlying systems are proven.
Principle: prototype risk before scaling content.
Principle: no content department should produce at final volume for a system whose runtime behavior has not passed a vertical-slice test.
Principle: every phase has entry dependencies and exit gates.
---
# ROADMAP OVERVIEW
Phase 0 — Canon, architecture, repository, and state tooling.
Phase 1 — Movement, camera, interaction, save skeleton, combat sandbox.
Phase 2 — Combat vertical slice and Tutorial Knight.
Phase 3 — Core RPG progression, equipment, inventory, loot, crafting skeleton.
Phase 4 — Companion runtime, relationship state, camp, dialogue scheduler.
Phase 5 — Quest/state engine, WorldClock, NPC schedules, consequence propagation.
Phase 6 — Economy, shops, reputation, factions, conduct profile.
Phase 7 — Open-world traversal, map, fast travel, Oakhaven production slice.
Phase 8 — Enemy ecology, farming, hunts, optional bosses.
Phase 9 — Ironhold production slice and cross-region systems.
Phase 10 — Wastes + Forgotten Sectors production.
Phase 11 — Mirror City + Cathedral Server production.
Phase 12 — Memory Ocean + Saved Assembly production.
Phase 13 — Human Patch Lab + Root of Heaven production.
Phase 14 — 27-route ending machinery and Story+.
Phase 15 — Full-content integration, balance, accessibility, localization readiness.
Phase 16 — Automated route/state QA, performance, save migration, release candidate.
Post-launch — only after launch architecture is stable.
---

Goal: make the project safe to expand.
Dependencies: none.
Build:

save version field.
event/state bus.

state inspector.

content validation scripts.
canonical data ownership rules.
separate runtime data from prose documentation.
Do not implement 150 quests yet.
Do not author final loot tables yet.

Quests.

No duplicate stable IDs.

# PHASE 1 — CONTROL FEEL FOUNDATION
Goal: prove movement and interaction feel good before building RPG complexity.

Build:
player movement.

dash.
camera.
interaction targeting.
pickup interaction.
basic hitboxes/hurtboxes.
basic enemy dummy.
health.

simple checkpoint/retry.

input remapping architecture.

## Phase 1 rule
No skill tree.
No rarity system.
No companion AI.

## Phase 1 acceptance tests
Movement feels responsive at 30/60/120 FPS targets where supported.
Input buffering works.
Dash timing is deterministic.
Collision does not trap player on common geometry.
Interaction prompt selects intended target.
Camera does not fight the player.
Controller and keyboard produce equivalent actions.
Death/retry restores player reliably.

## Phase 1 exit gate
A tester can move for ten minutes without fighting the controls.
If movement is merely acceptable, keep iterating.

guard.

shield bash or guard break.
stagger/posture.
one status effect.
basic Root action.
Root corruption prototype.
healing item.
three enemy archetypes.
Aldric Tutorial Knight production-quality prototype.
combat HUD.
boss retry flow.
hit pause.
sound feedback.
camera feedback.
telegraphs.

Melee pressure enemy.
Ranged/spacing enemy.

Story.

inventory.
stash.
quick items.
loot.

# PERFORMANCE BUDGET RULE
Large narrative scope does not justify uncontrolled runtime cost.
NPC AI outside active radius should use lightweight simulation.
Dialogue databases should stream/index rather than remain fully active.
World-state changes should use event-driven updates where possible.
Enemy populations outside active zones should not run full combat AI.
Pathfinding must be profiled in dense hubs.
Save files must store state compactly rather than serializing entire live scene trees.
---
# CONTENT PRODUCTION RULE
Do not fully author/animate/content-fill every planned subregion before the first production region passes blind tests.
Expansion follows demonstrated fun.
A weak subregion is cut or redesigned.
The master is permission to build, not an obligation to ship every optional idea.

# SCOPE GATES
Gate 1: movement fun.
Gate 2: combat fun.
Gate 3: build variety fun.
Gate 4: companion useful and likable.
Gate 5: Oakhaven feels alive.
Gate 6: consequences are noticed.
Gate 7: Ironhold proves second-region scalability.
Gate 8: Wastes proves changing geography.
Gate 9: Null Court proves noncombat systemic storytelling.
Gate 10: late-game axes remain understandable.
Gate 11: final bosses work mechanically and emotionally.
Gate 12: at least several routes feel meaningfully different in blind playtests.
Only after each gate passes should corresponding content scale aggressively.
---
# POST-LAUNCH / LONG-TERM RULE
Post-launch expansions may add:
new regions.
new companions.
new weapon family.
new mystery layers.
new Story+ crises.
new outside-world contact.
new superbosses.
They should plug into stable state interfaces.
They should not retroactively make base-game endings invalid.
The base game must remain emotionally complete.
---
# ROADMAP FINAL PRINCIPLE
The build order is:
prove feel.
prove systems.
prove one living region.
prove cross-region state.
then scale content.
Do not reverse that order.
The largest risk to Aethelgard is not lack of ideas.
The largest risk is producing thousands of assets and scenes before the systems carrying them are stable and fun.

# DIALOGUE PRODUCTION REPLACEMENT — CANONICAL
Status: replaces the deleted bulk-generated companion, ambient, and Tier B stateful dialogue banks.
Purpose: preserve state coverage without shipping repetitive template prose.

# COMPANION DIALOGUE STANDARD
Companion dialogue is authored by scene intention, current relationship state, and immediate desire.
Do not generate a conversation by inserting a topic into a fixed sentence template.
The relationship matrix remains valid.
The exact spoken line is not pre-generated for every matrix cell.
A matrix state changes:
what the companion volunteers.
what they challenge.
how long they stay in the conversation.
whether they believe Kaelen's explanation.
whether they ask permission.
whether they interrupt.
whether they joke.
whether they leave.
whether silence is comfortable.
---
# ELARA DIALOGUE BRIEF
Core desire: protect ordinary people without becoming a tool everyone feels entitled to use.
Ordinary interests: food, village gossip, herbal work, small competitions, repairs, weather.
Humor: dry, practical, sometimes competitive.
Avoid: turning every arm conversation into a consent lecture.
Low Trust: verifies details and avoids vulnerable admissions.
High Trust: lets Kaelen see fear and exhaustion without asking him to fix them.
Low Respect: interrupts when Kaelen starts solving before listening.
High Respect: disagrees directly because she expects disagreement to be safe.
High Reliance: may resent needing Kaelen and test whether she can solve something without him.
Example:
ELARA: You moved the chair.
KAELEN: It was in the way.
ELARA: It was my way.
KAELEN: Important distinction.
ELARA: Learning.
Example:
ELARA: My arm is bad today.
KAELEN: Do you want help.
ELARA: I want soup.
KAELEN: Different department.
ELARA: Best department.
---
# SERAPHINA DIALOGUE BRIEF
Core desire: keep people alive without becoming indispensable commander forever.
Ordinary interests: routines, exits, sleep, crew habits, tea, badly folded clothes.
Humor: controlled and unexpectedly literal.
Avoid: making every line about duty.
Low Trust: withholds operational vulnerabilities.
High Trust: admits uncertainty before it becomes crisis.
Low Respect: gives Kaelen instructions instead of asking.
High Respect: accepts being questioned publicly.
High Reliance: must confront the fact that relying on Kaelen can resemble the command hierarchy she distrusts.
Example:
SERAPHINA: I slept six hours.
KAELEN: Congratulations.
SERAPHINA: Do not patronize me.
KAELEN: I was genuinely impressed.
SERAPHINA: Worse.
---
# LYRA DIALOGUE BRIEF
Core desire: decide what memory means without being reduced to what she can recover.
Ordinary interests: stationery, tea, cataloging mistakes, handwriting, quiet walks.
Humor: understated, literal, occasionally self-directed.
Avoid: every memory mistake becoming tragic.
Low Trust: records Kaelen's claims instead of accepting them.
High Trust: shares uncertainty without immediately checking notes.
Low Respect: treats Kaelen as another person who wants a clean version of her.
High Respect: lets him witness contradiction without needing him to resolve it.
Example:
LYRA: I wrote that I hate this tea.
KAELEN: Yesterday you said you liked it.
LYRA: Yesterday me was free to be wrong.
---
# KAELTHAS DIALOGUE BRIEF
Core desire: make concealed power visible without becoming another person who controls truth.
Ordinary interests: catalog systems, public arguments, bad indexing, old books, being right.
Humor: sharp and often accidental.
Avoid: making him a permanent exposition machine.
Low Trust: assumes Kaelen's omissions are strategic.
High Trust: asks before publishing personal material.
Low Respect: tries to force disclosure.
High Respect: argues procedure instead of overriding people.
Example:
KAELTHAS: Your archive has three labels for the same event.
LYRA: Four.
KAELTHAS: I am trying to be kind.
---
# KAITO DIALOGUE BRIEF
Core desire: keep moving and discovering without turning places into possessions.
Ordinary interests: views, road names, bad maps, camp food, improvised gear.
Humor: playful and geographic.
Avoid: every line being a map joke.
Low Trust: hides routes that might be abused.
High Trust: shares unfinished maps.
Low Respect: treats Kaelen's plan as another landmark to route around.
High Respect: asks before publicizing discoveries.
Example:
KAITO: Good news.
KAELEN: There is a road.
KAITO: There was.
KAELEN: And the good news.
KAITO: We know where it isn't.
---
# SEVEN DIALOGUE BRIEF
Core desire: discover preferences that are not disguised directives.
Ordinary interests: maintenance, sunrise, naming, sounds, tools, inefficient hobbies.
Humor: literal statements that become intentional over time.
Avoid: turning every sentence into machine comedy.
Low Trust: requests clarification before accepting Kaelen's motives.
High Trust: admits preference without rationalizing it.
Low Respect: interprets Kaelen's requests as likely commands.
High Respect: distinguishes request, advice, and order confidently.
Example:
SEVEN: I have purchased a cup.
KAELEN: You do not drink.
SEVEN: Correct.
KAELEN: Why.
SEVEN: I liked it.
Pause.
SEVEN: This remains inefficient.
---
# NEMA DIALOGUE BRIEF
Core desire: live as a person rather than as the argument everyone uses about deleted citizens.
Ordinary interests: food, clothes, active-district shops, jokes, annoyances, chosen names.
Humor: direct and impatient.
Avoid: making her explain personhood in every scene.
Low Trust: challenges Kaelen's wording before his intent.
High Trust: asks him ordinary favors.
Low Respect: assumes he will make her into an example.
High Respect: lets him speak for himself while retaining the right to correct him.
Example:
NEMA: Stop looking at me like I am historically significant.
KAELEN: You are holding a court seal from a deleted century.
NEMA: It is also keeping the table level.
---
# ROOK DIALOGUE BRIEF
Core desire: survive systems of scarcity without pretending cost disappears when nobody mentions it.
Ordinary interests: food, bets, clothes, market rumors, bad purchases, useful junk.
Humor: transactional until suddenly sincere.
Avoid: making every sentence an economics metaphor.
Low Trust: prices Kaelen's promises as risk.
High Trust: helps without negotiating and hates being noticed.
Low Respect: assumes idealism will leave someone else paying.
High Respect: asks who bears cost instead of dismissing the idea.
Example:
ROOK: I bought this cheaply.
KAELEN: It is broken.
ROOK: That is why it was cheap.
KAELEN: Strong system.
ROOK: You are learning.

# COMPANION PAIR DYNAMICS
Elara / Seraphina: local care versus command discipline; mutual respect through practical work.
Elara / Lyra: quiet companionship; neither forces the other to explain pain.
Elara / Kaelthas: friction over public truth versus personal boundaries.
Elara / Kaito: playful competitiveness.
Elara / Seven: Elara teaches informal preference without treating Seven as a child.
Elara / Nema: fast friendship based on disliking being turned into symbols.
Elara / Rook: constant argument about price versus need; surprisingly effective teamwork.
Seraphina / Lyra: shared habit of counting and recording; different relationship to uncertainty.
Seraphina / Kaelthas: command secrecy versus disclosure.
Seraphina / Kaito: safety planning versus improvisation.
Seraphina / Seven: operational respect; both understand systems and end conditions.
Seraphina / Nema: person-first challenges to command language.
Seraphina / Rook: logistics arguments.
Lyra / Kaelthas: closest ideological conflict inside Archive thinking.
Lyra / Kaito: maps versus notes; uncertainty treated as normal.
Lyra / Seven: identity through continuity without requiring perfect memory.
Lyra / Nema: shared refusal of canonical versions.
Lyra / Rook: Rook wants actionable answer; Lyra refuses false certainty.
Kaelthas / Kaito: publication versus protected locations.
Kaelthas / Seven: whether transparent logs can themselves become coercive.
Kaelthas / Nema: truth versus privacy at maximum pressure.
Kaelthas / Rook: both cynical for different reasons.
Kaito / Seven: exploration through map and system senses.
Kaito / Nema: new places and active-district curiosity.
Kaito / Rook: scavenger-market comedy.
Seven / Nema: two people repeatedly misclassified by systems.
Seven / Rook: efficiency language versus actual value.
Nema / Rook: both notice who policy quietly burdens.
---
# COMPANION BARK STANDARD
Combat barks are short.
A bark describes immediate danger, tactic, reaction, or relationship.
Do not use combat barks to restate philosophy.
No companion should have the same bark text assigned to five unrelated trigger types.
Bark cooldown prevents repetition.
Priority order:
critical warning.
companion down.
civilian danger.
boss mechanic.
rare relationship reaction.
ordinary combat praise/complaint.
Low-priority bark may be suppressed entirely.
---
# TIER B NPC DIALOGUE STANDARD
The existing 70 Tier B NPC identity briefs remain canonical.
Their deleted bulk stateful dialogue bank is not canonical spoken text.
Every Tier B NPC receives during implementation:
one immediate personal desire.
one ongoing practical problem.
one relationship to another named NPC.
one non-story interest.
one regional opinion.
one thing they misunderstand.
one thing they know better than Kaelen.
one state that changes their schedule.
one state that can move or remove them.
three to eight bespoke conversations across the game.
additional short barks as needed.
Not every Tier B NPC needs a conversation for every faction/authority/deleted-policy combination.
Only write a response when that state actually touches their life.
---
# TIER B EXAMPLE — BRAN FEN
Immediate desire: keep the gate staffed without returning to permanent military life.
Practical problem: bridge traffic has doubled.
Relationship: owes Mara for feeding guards during the first Fracture winter.
Non-story interest: repairs old whistles badly.
Misunderstanding: assumes most system labels are weather notation.
Expertise: knows who actually travels through Oakhaven and when.
State change: refugee surge moves him from gate to temporary housing coordination.
Dialogue:
BRAN: Gate count is wrong.
KAELEN: By how much.
BRAN: Depends whether goats are citizens.
KAELEN: Dangerous question here.
BRAN: Then tell Pebbles to stop crossing four times.
---
# TIER B EXAMPLE — MARA QUILL
Immediate desire: keep feeding people without turning kindness into permanent debt.
Practical problem: flour supply and kitchen capacity.
Relationship: protective of Elara, competitive with Rook over prices.
Non-story interest: terrible singing while baking.
Expertise: knows who is hungry before officials do.
State change: Story+ can transform bakery into community kitchen or private cooperative.
Dialogue:
MARA: Take the bread.
KAELEN: I can pay.
MARA: Then pay tomorrow.
KAELEN: Why tomorrow.
MARA: Because today you look like a problem.
---
# TIER B EXAMPLE — REM ILYAR
Immediate desire: keep medicine available without becoming emergency government by default.
Practical problem: rotating shortages.
Relationship: trusts Seraphina's judgment more than her work habits.
Non-story interest: collects useless arena tickets.
Expertise: actual medical capacity.
State change: medicine crisis moves him between clinic and supply depot.
Dialogue:
REM: No.
KAELEN: I have not asked yet.
REM: You are bleeding on my clean floor.
KAELEN: Fair.
REM: That one you can keep.
---
# TIER B EXAMPLE — HESSA VANE
Immediate desire: run a normal business in a district everyone else keeps calling abnormal.
Practical problem: customer records changing after reintegration.
Relationship: likes Nema; finds Ilyen's forms offensive aesthetically.
Non-story interest: gossip and hairstyle competitions.
Expertise: hears how ordinary residents describe policy when officials leave.
Dialogue:

KAELEN: I do not need a haircut.
HESSA: Then stop having hair.

# TIER B EXAMPLE — SISTER OSSA
Immediate desire: make care available without repeating Mercy's coercion.
Practical problem: too few clinicians.
Relationship: patient with Seven; impatient with Kaelen's self-neglect.
Non-story interest: grows medicinal flowers badly.
Expertise: pain, consent under distress, clinic logistics.
Dialogue:

KAELEN: Several people have mentioned that.
OSSA: Good. Saves me time.

# TIER B EXAMPLE — TAVI RENN
Immediate desire: make civic work function without becoming another permanent political class.
Practical problem: everyone uses runners instead of fixing communication systems.
Relationship: knows almost every delegate and trusts very few schedules.
Non-story interest: collects badly printed notices.
Expertise: actual information flow across the Assembly.
Dialogue:
TAVI: Message.
KAELEN: For me.
TAVI: Unfortunately.
KAELEN: From.
TAVI: Three committees.
KAELEN: Same message.
TAVI: Three different punctuation choices.

# TIER C NPC RUNTIME DIALOGUE SYSTEM — CANONICAL
Status: replaces the deleted 36k-line templated Tier C reaction corpus.
Purpose: preserve 200 living NPCs without making 200 people repeat the same twenty sentences.
---
# TIER C PRINCIPLE
Tier C NPCs are short-form world-reactive residents.
They are not miniature companions.
They should feel specific enough to belong in the world and light enough to maintain.
The existing C001–C200 identity definitions remain canonical.
Their role, region, schedule model, local-memory topic, secondary topic, and Story+ topic remain valid.
---
# TIER C DIALOGUE SOURCES
A Tier C line comes from five layers.
Layer 1: personal micro-profile.
Layer 2: occupation voice pack.
Layer 3: regional voice pack.
Layer 4: current local-state reaction.
Layer 5: ordinary-life fallback.
The runtime never constructs important dialogue by concatenating arbitrary nouns into generic sentences.
Critical dialogue is always authored.
---
# TIER C PERSONAL MICRO-PROFILE
Each Tier C NPC receives:
one ordinary want.
one ordinary irritation.
one person they know.
one preferred place.
one schedule variation.
one local event they remember.
one thing they are bad at.
one thing they are proud of.
This can be stored as data, not exposed as exposition.
---
# OCCUPATION VOICE PACKS
Farm worker.
Speaks concretely about weather, soil, tools, transport, labor, and food.
Avoids abstract policy language unless policy changes work directly.
---
Guard.
Speaks through routes, people, timing, risk, and rules.
Does not automatically support authority.
---
Merchant.
Speaks through stock, customers, reputation, shortages, and opportunity.
Does not turn every event into greed.
---
Healer aide.
Speaks through time, capacity, pain, supply, and people waiting.
Avoids philosophical medical monologues unless in authored scene.
---
Teacher / school worker.
Speaks through children, routine, attendance, questions, and family behavior.
---
Worker / craftsperson.
Speaks through material, tools, repairs, quality, time, and coworkers.
---
Archivist / clerk.
Speaks through records, mistakes, queue order, provenance, and administrative inconvenience.
Avoids sounding like Kaelthas.
---
Courier / runner.
Speaks through distance, timing, roads, who is waiting, and message reliability.
---
Cook / food worker.
Speaks through ingredients, hunger, waste, preference, and community routine.
---
Transport worker.
Speaks through route, schedule, capacity, maintenance, and passenger behavior.
---
