# LOCAL-STATE REACTION RULE
Tier C NPCs react only when they have a reason to know.
Examples:
bridge worker can discuss bridge closure.
remote Cathedral cook does not automatically know a private Null Court ruling.
News propagation has delays.
Faction propaganda may distort information.
Rumor can differ from fact.
---
# STATE REACTION LENGTH
One to three lines normally.
Four to six only when an NPC has personal involvement.
If the state requires a longer conversation, promote the NPC temporarily to authored Tier B scene treatment.
---
# REPEAT CONTROL
A Tier C state reaction normally fires once.
Afterward the NPC returns to ordinary-life barks until state changes.
No player can press interact fifty times to exhaust a giant hidden dialogue tree.
---
# TIER C STORY+ RULE
Story+ changes visible routines first.
Dialogue follows the routine.
Examples:
new shift.
closed stall.
different route.
new customer queue.
changed uniform.
different opening hours.
new roommate.
Only then does the NPC comment.
This keeps world reaction from becoming a wall of exposition.
---
# TIER C QUALITY GATE
Before a Tier C NPC ships:
their name/role/schedule are valid.
their lines match region.
their lines match occupation.
their lines do not duplicate another nearby NPC's exact joke.
their state reaction references a fact they could know.
their dialogue does not contain critical lore unavailable elsewhere.
their ordinary-life bark exists.
---
# END TIER C NPC RUNTIME DIALOGUE SYSTEM
---
# PRODUCTION SCOPE NORMALIZATION
Status: CANONICAL.
Purpose: preserve ambition without converting every catalogued idea into a mandatory launch burden.
---
# MASTER CONTENT IS A RESERVOIR
The master contains more content than the game is obligated to ship simultaneously.
Catalog count is not a quality metric.
A listed quest, subregion, NPC, activity, weapon family, or optional system may be:
launch content.
Story+ content.
New Game Plus content.
post-launch expansion content.
cut after testing.
merged with stronger content.
Its existence in the master means it is available to production, not that weak implementation must be shipped to satisfy a number.
---
# NON-NEGOTIABLE LAUNCH CORE
Ten-chapter critical path.
Four-act structure.
Eight core region identities.
Eight major companion arcs.
Seven Source Key domains.
SOVEREIGN.
God King.
Three authority approaches.
Three faction approaches.
Three deleted-person approaches.
Twenty-four standard storyline outcomes.
Three secret storyline transformations.
A complete first-playthrough emotional ending.
A playable Story+ foundation.
---
# QUALITY-GATED CONTENT POOLS
Side-quest catalog: up to 150 authored entries.
Secret-quest catalog: up to 30.
Time-sensitive catalog: up to 40.
Tier B NPC pool: 70.
Tier C NPC pool: approximately 200.
Expanded subregion pool: up to roughly 80 concepts.
These are ceilings/reservoirs, not quotas.
Every shipped item must pass density, uniqueness, technical, and pacing gates.
---
# REGION SHIPPING RULE
Every core region ships with enough surrounding world to feel geographically and socially real.
There is no fixed requirement that all ten proposed subregions per region launch.
Start with the strongest.
Expand only when:
traversal is fun.
content density remains healthy.
performance remains acceptable.
the new area adds a distinct function.
Open-world size is earned by quality.
---
# QUEST SHIPPING RULE
A side quest ships only if it accomplishes at least one of:
strong character scene.
meaningful world consequence.
unique gameplay.
regional culture.
mystery discovery.
mechanical reward.
humor or emotional texture strong enough to justify itself.
A quest that exists only to increase quest count is cut or merged.
---
# NPC SHIPPING RULE
An NPC does not need a personal quest to justify existence.
They do need:
a world function.
a schedule or believable presence.
region-appropriate behavior.
at least one ordinary-life identity marker.
If two NPCs perform the same narrative function with weaker writing, merge them.
---
# WEAPON SHIPPING RULE
Do not ship a weapon family until its moveset feels meaningfully different.
Three excellent families are better than ten weak families.
The master may retain future weapon concepts.
---
# ENDING SHIPPING RULE
All 27 storyline IDs remain part of the launch architecture.
They do not require 27 entirely separate final acts.
They require:
clear route identity.
meaningful route-conditioned climax.
distinct ending composition.
distinct Story+ problem.
This preserves replayability without multiplying the entire game by twenty-seven.
---
# VOICE-ACTING RULE
Full voice acting is not assumed by the canonical narrative.
If budget supports only partial voice:
voice critical path.
major companion scenes.
major bosses.
key Story+ scenes.
Ambient/Tier C may remain text with expressive sound design.
Do not reduce writing quality merely to fit voice budget.
---
# QUALITY OVER COUNT
The game is not judged by:
word count.
quest count.
NPC count.
map area.
weapon count.
ending count in isolation.
The game is judged by what the player actually experiences.
---
# END PRODUCTION SCOPE NORMALIZATION
# HYBRID PERSPECTIVE RISK PATCH
Status: CANONICAL PROTOTYPE GATE.
The current genre contract proposes top-down exploration and side-scrolling action combat.
This is a distinctive idea, but it is also a high-risk production choice because open-world farming, random encounters, traversal, camera logic, enemy spawning, animation, and level design must work across two spatial models.
The hybrid format is therefore a prototype hypothesis, not an untouchable requirement.
---
# REQUIRED PROTOTYPE COMPARISON
Before building multiple regions, compare:
Option A — all combat transitions into side-view combat spaces.
Option B — top-down field combat with side-view authored boss / major encounter arenas.
Option C — top-down exploration with seamless local camera/perspective shifts only where geometry supports them.
Evaluate:
flow interruption.
encounter frequency.
grinding comfort.
enemy variety.
camera clarity.
animation workload.
level-design workload.
companion AI.
backtracking.
boss quality.
controller feel.
---
# DECISION RULE
If full side-view transitions make ordinary farmable encounters feel repetitive or slow, use top-down field combat and reserve side-view combat for major authored encounters.
If seamless hybrid combat is genuinely more fun in blind tests, retain it.
The narrative does not depend on one camera perspective.
Combat quality overrides format loyalty.
---
# TRANSITION RULE
If combat changes perspective:
transition must be fast.
player position must remain understandable.
return position must be deterministic.
no hidden loading-feeling pause.
no enemy encounter should trap the player in repeated transition loops.
players must be able to avoid some field encounters through movement.
---
# END HYBRID PERSPECTIVE RISK PATCH
# FINAL CANON PRECEDENCE & HIGH-RISK INTERACTION PATCH
Status: HIGHEST AUTHORITY INSIDE THIS MASTER.
If two parts of the master conflict, use the following precedence.
1. FINAL CANON PRECEDENCE & HIGH-RISK INTERACTION PATCH.
2. FINAL GAME-SYSTEMS AUDIT & ENHANCEMENT CONTRACT.
3. IMPLEMENTATION ROADMAP.
4. OPEN-WORLD DECOMPRESSION & NARRATIVE DELIVERY.
5. FINAL CANONICAL SCENE INSERTS.
6. FINAL RED-TEAM NARRATIVE REVIEW / CANON PATCHES.
7. STORY+ FINAL ROUTE-SPECIFIC VERSION.
8. Chapter/quest/character specifications.
9. Older examples, prototype dialogue, or historical review text.
A later section does not override an earlier higher-precedence section merely because it appears later in the file.
Historical scorecards are commentary, not canon.
Prototype examples illustrate intent unless explicitly marked REQUIRED.
---
# RELATIONSHIP STATE EXPLOSION SAFEGUARD
Trust, Respect, and Reliance remain three independent dimensions.
The 27 theoretical combinations per companion are a behavior model.
Production does not require unique dialogue for every combination multiplied by every route, faction, timing state, and region.
Scenes query only the dimensions relevant to that scene.
Example:
a confession scene may query Trust.
a disagreement scene may query Respect.
a dependency scene may query Reliance.
a rare climax may query two or all three.
This prevents combinatorial content explosion while preserving psychological depth.
---
# TIMED-QUEST ANXIETY SAFEGUARD
WorldClock deadlines use game-world time, not hidden real-world seconds unless a scene explicitly presents a short immediate countdown.
World time does not advance while the game is paused.
Menus do not consume deadline time unless clearly stated for a special simulation feature.
Travel previews show expected time cost when a deadline is active.
Critical deadlines provide at least one warning before irreversible closure when fiction allows.
Difficulty/accessibility options may widen windows.
Exploration should not feel punished simply because the player stopped to look around.
Tier 4/5 quests and secret-route prerequisites do not silently auto-resolve offscreen without prior warning or an explicitly authored reason.
---
# CORRUPTION FAIRNESS SAFEGUARD
High Root corruption may distort:
visual labels.
noncritical environmental interpretation.
optional memory presentation.
selected combat tactics.
It must not:
lie about irreversible choice text.
falsify accessibility telegraphs.
hide mandatory quest objectives without an alternative.
change save files secretly.
make a critical NPC appear hostile in a way that tricks the player into unavoidable permanent loss.
If perception is unreliable, the game communicates that unreliability.
---
# FINAL-BOSS PACING SAFEGUARD
SOVEREIGN is the emotional penultimate climax.
God King is the structural final climax.
The player receives a checkpoint between them.
Core consumables and critical resources are restored enough that failure against God King does not force replay of SOVEREIGN.
God King should not simply have more health and more phases than SOVEREIGN.
Its fight is shorter or differently structured around the authority mechanic.
The transition includes time for the player to understand that the new process is not a random second villain.
If SOVEREIGN survives, its participation helps differentiate the encounter emotionally.
---
# GOD KING PRODUCTION SAFEGUARD
The God King uses a shared combat core plus route modifiers.
Do not implement twenty-seven completely separate bosses.
Shared core target: roughly sixty to seventy percent of mechanics/animation.
Authority axis changes the major final-permission mechanic.
Faction axis changes support/arena logic.
Deleted-person axis changes the personhood phase.
Secret routes replace selected final logic.
This preserves meaningful thematic gameplay without twenty-seven-fold boss production.
---
# NPC AUTONOMY SAFEGUARD
NPCs may solve ordinary and regional problems without Kaelen.
They may not silently resolve:
main-story defining choices.
companion climax choices.
secret-ending critical decisions.
irreversible Tier 5 decisions.
unless the player was explicitly warned that time/inaction would hand the decision to others.
NPC autonomy makes the world alive.
It must not make the player feel arbitrarily excluded from the game they are playing.
---
# MICRO-EVENT DETERMINISM
Dynamic micro-events use controlled pools and persistent state.
Save/load must not endlessly reroll the same event for exploit.
Rare events may use deterministic seeded selection or persistent cooldowns.
No critical progression relies on random micro-event appearance.
---
# TERMINOLOGY ACCESSIBILITY
Critical concepts are introduced in plain language before or alongside specialist terms.
Do not introduce multiple new system terms in one conversation unless the scene is explicitly technical.
Journal/Help can define:
Root.
Fracture.
continuity.
restoration.
release.
provenance.
Human Patch.
Source Key.
No player should need the codex to understand what a major choice physically does.
---
# END FINAL CANON PRECEDENCE & HIGH-RISK INTERACTION PATCH

# WHAT IS GENUINELY EXCELLENT
The strongest element remains the distinction between capability and legitimacy.
Source Key progression gives Kaelen power without giving him automatic moral authority.
This supports story, politics, boss mechanics, companions, and endings.
---
SOVEREIGN remains the strongest antagonist.
Its preservation motive is understandable.
Its fear is justified.
Its error is permanent jurisdiction.
The story allows SOVEREIGN to perform compassionate actions without erasing its coercion.
That is substantially stronger than an evil-system antagonist.
---
The God King now works as a structural climax rather than a surprise bigger villain.
Foreshadowing exists.
SOVEREIGN suppresses the role rather than secretly being identical to it.
The fight mechanically interrogates the player's chosen authority model.
---
The Null Court / Nema material gives the abstract world a human legal and emotional test.
The story does not rely only on cosmic reveals.
---
The ordinary-life scenes remain some of the best material.
Chair.
mug.
bread.
tea.
sleep.
bad purchases.
orange.
games.
maps.
These justify the political stakes emotionally.
---
The route architecture is highly replayable without requiring twenty-seven totally separate games.
The three-axis composition is sophisticated and understandable once introduced gradually.
---
# PLOT-HOLE AUDIT
No major unresolved plot hole was found in the current canonical hierarchy.
Previously dangerous gaps have explicit answers:
Seraphina / Kaelen arrival-time mismatch.
Kaelen quarantine.
Kaelen Root access.
seven Source domains.
SOVEREIGN inability to simply delete Kaelen.
SOVEREIGN's reason for withholding history.
native-born / local-emergent people.
magic after the technical reveal.
Elara's arm complexity.
Root corruption.
SOVEREIGN / God King relationship.
outside-signal evidentiary limits.
Routine player defeat versus canonical restoration.
Remaining unknowns are intentionally unknown or production-tunable:
exact Earth condition.
exact outside elapsed time.
exact global population.
Mira's final relationship definition.
some final numeric thresholds.
These are not currently logic holes.
---
# MYSTERY REVIEW
The story correctly stopped treating "this world is computational" as the main surprise.
That reveal is too guessable.
The real mystery ladder is stronger:
why Kaelen is delayed.
why SOVEREIGN knows him.
why seven domains recognize him.
what happened outside.
why crown/resolver traces predate SOVEREIGN.
what legitimate authority means after preservation.
This is fair mystery rather than narrator deception.
Risk:
technical terminology can still make some reveals feel intellectual rather than emotional.
Safeguard:
plain-language terminology rule and ordinary character stakes.
---
# CHARACTER REVIEW
Kaelen is good but not the strongest character yet.
Risk:
he can become the neutral conversational center around more distinctive companions.
Required production focus:
give Kaelen specific tastes, habits, irritations, failures, Earth memories, and desires beyond responsibility.
He must sometimes want something selfish, ordinary, or embarrassing.
His desire to go home must remain emotionally active.
---
Elara:
strong emotional anchor.
Risk:
overuse as moral common sense.
Counter:
she must be wrong sometimes and make decisions others challenge.
---
Seraphina:
strong.
Timeline asymmetry creates identity.
Risk:
command/duty language could dominate.
Counter:
sleep, crew memories, humor, ordinary preferences.
---
Lyra:
strong and distinctive.
Risk:
memory uncertainty could become repetitive sadness.
Counter:
ordinary mistakes, preference change, curiosity, humor.
---
Kaelthas:
useful ideological friction.
Risk:
becoming exposition/disclosure machine.
Counter:
privacy growth and ordinary arrogance.
---
Kaito:
good tonal pressure release.
Risk:
map jokes becoming gimmick.
Counter:
places, fear of attachment, protected communities, exploration.
---
Seven:
very strong.
Risk:
literal-machine humor can become predictable.
Counter:
develop deliberate humor, taste, aesthetic preference, annoyance.
---
Nema:
very strong.
Risk:
becoming personhood spokesperson.
Counter:
ordinary active-district life and refusal to be symbolic.
---
Rook:
valuable because economy/material cost is otherwise easy to ignore.
Risk:
every line becoming price joke.
Counter:
irrational generosity and personal taste.

The biggest old defect was bulk repetition.
That defect was materially reduced during this audit by deleting:
old templated Tier B stateful dialogue.
old mass-generated companion conversation banks.
old 960-exchange ambient bank.
old 36k-line Tier C reaction corpus.
These were replaced by behavior rules, regional voice packs, and authored examples.
This makes the master smaller and better.
The master should never again use raw line count as a quality target.

the Trust/Respect/Reliance matrix contains illustrative repeated lines.

Runtime dialogue must be authored for scene need.

Act 4 can become emotionally exhausting.

field missions between votes.
ordinary life after thematic scenes.
SOVEREIGN / God King checkpoint.
God King structural rather than HP escalation.

measure actual minutes between high-intensity dialogue scenes.
Do not rely on page count.

Very strong.

relationships.
regions.
timing.
economy.
quest availability.
evidence.
boss support.
faction standing.
ending composition.
Story+.
This exceeds cosmetic-choice design.
The strongest rule is that failure can create content.
That should survive implementation.
---
# SIDE-QUEST REVIEW
Strong architecture.
The best side quests change local life or reveal character.
The risk is catalog pressure.
A 150-quest catalog must not become 150 mandatory production promises.
Quality-gated reservoir rule fixes this.
Mutually exclusive quests and consequence quests improve replayability.
---
# ENDINGS / ROUTES REVIEW
Design quality is high.
Production danger is high.
The fix is compositional architecture.
Twenty-seven route IDs remain.
Twenty-seven full independent final acts do not.
Story+ signature crises are route-specific.
The repeated SP coverage beats are a checklist, not mandatory identical scene order.
This distinction must be respected in implementation.
---
# OPEN-WORLD REVIEW
The decompression direction is correct.
Bigger world can improve the story if it creates:
more life.
regional difference.
exploration.
ordinary activity.
consequence space.
It becomes harmful if it creates:
empty travel.
repeated camps.
enemy spam.
checklist markers.
The subregion list is therefore a reservoir.
Blind tests decide actual shipping density.
---
# COMBAT REVIEW
The intended combat values are good:
commitment.
readable dodge.
parry.
guard break.
stagger.
Root risk.
build diversity.
boss mechanics tied to story.
The largest unresolved gameplay question is perspective.
Top-down exploration plus universal side-view combat may be excellent or irritating.
The hybrid perspective patch correctly makes this a prototype gate.
Do not build regions around an unproven transition system.
---
# PROGRESSION REVIEW
The new progression specification is appropriately restrained.
Six-ish attributes.
compact skill families.
respec.
weapon identity.
limited rarity.
no durability.
no affix explosion.
This fits Aethelgard better than a loot treadmill.
Risk:
too many systems can still compete for attention.
Rule:
new systems unlock gradually.
---
# ENEMY / FARMING REVIEW
The farming system now has a coherent purpose.
Grinding is optional preparation.
Drops have deterministic alternatives.
Enemy ecology reacts to world state.
This is good.
Risk:
if field combat uses forced side-view transitions, frequent farming may become tedious.
Prototype this early.
---
# ECONOMY REVIEW
Economy is one of the more distinctive supporting systems.
Prices react to actual world events.
Rook gives it character.
Good decision:
one main currency.
conditional special currencies.
no morality score.
Risk:
over-simulation.
Keep price changes category-based and understandable.
---
# MORALITY / REPUTATION REVIEW
Rejecting Good/Evil is correct.
Conduct dimensions are much more compatible with the story.
Regional reputation and faction standing provide social consequence.
Risk:
hidden conduct values can feel manipulative if they secretly decide huge outcomes.
Rule:
conduct influences interpretation/dialogue/access.
Major route choices remain explicit player decisions.
---
# TIME / WORLD SIMULATION REVIEW
WorldClock is valuable because timing produces different states.
Risk:
open-world players become afraid to explore.
The timed-quest safeguard is required.
Most exploration should remain safe from hidden deadlines.
---
# SAVE / STATE REVIEW
The new architecture is strong.
Manual saves.
rolling autosaves.
pre-lock autosaves.
versioned schema.
migration.
state inspector.
automated route tests.
For a game this stateful, this is not polish.
It is core architecture.
---
# ACCESSIBILITY REVIEW
Specification is now strong at design level.
It aligns with established accessibility practice:
remapping.
subtitle controls.
separate audio.
color-independent cues.
timing assists.
autosave/manual save.
practice/tutorial review.
Risk:
accessibility is often postponed.
Roadmap correctly requires architecture early.
---
# TECHNICAL REVIEW
Godot 4.6 is capable of this style of 2D project in principle.
The technical challenge is not rendering.
It is state complexity.
Primary technical risks:
save schema.
quest graph.
NPC scheduling.
hybrid perspective.
companion navigation.
large dialogue indexing.
route eligibility.
Story+ migration.
performance in dense hubs.
Automated tests and debug tools are correctly Phase 0.
---
# MAINTAINABILITY REVIEW
The master used to be too monolithic and too repetitive.
It is now substantially cleaner.
The canonical source can remain one reference file.
Runtime production data should not.
Implementation must split:
dialogue.
quests.
NPCs.
items.
enemies.
routes.
economy.
world.
The precedence hierarchy is mandatory because the master contains historical review material.
---
# SCOPE REVIEW
This remains the weakest score.
Even with a ten-year horizon, the design is very large.
Eight regions.
eight companions.
large quest reservoir.
large NPC pool.
27 routes.
Story+.
NG+.
RPG systems.
open-world simulation.
The correct response is not deleting ambition from the master.
The correct response is production gates.
If Oakhaven is not excellent, do not build seven more mediocre regions.
If three weapons are not excellent, do not make ten.
If twenty side quests are not consistently strong, do not celebrate reaching 150.
---
# PRODUCTION FAILURE MODES
Failure mode 1:
content production begins before combat/state tooling stabilizes.
Result:
mass rewrite/rework.
Prevention:
roadmap gates.
---
Failure mode 2:
every NPC comments on every theme.
Result:
author voice replaces world voice.
Prevention:
desire-first dialogue and semantic cooldown.
---
Failure mode 3:
choices become invisible flag math.
Result:
player cannot understand consequence.
Prevention:
physical world changes, schedules, prices, people.
---
Failure mode 4:
27 routes become checklist recolors.
Result:
replayability feels artificial.
Prevention:
route-specific crises and asymmetrical Story+ forms.
---
Failure mode 5:
open world becomes empty.
Result:
size weakens pacing.
Prevention:
subregion quality gates.
---
Failure mode 6:
timed quests punish curiosity.
Result:
players stop exploring.
Prevention:
visible time costs and leniency.
---
Failure mode 7:
SOVEREIGN emotional climax is erased by God King spectacle.
Result:
finale feels like bait-and-switch.
Prevention:
short structural God King fight, checkpoint, SOVEREIGN aftermath/ally state.
---
Failure mode 8:
system count creates menu fatigue.
Result:
RPG feels like administration.
Prevention:
gradual unlocks, compact trees, limited currencies, restrained itemization.
---
Failure mode 9:
state bugs destroy trust.
Result:
NPCs reference impossible events or endings lock incorrectly.
Prevention:
automated story/state tests.
---
Failure mode 10:
AI-assisted content volume reintroduces template language.
Result:
quality falls invisibly.
Prevention:
duplication scans, voice review, human-style line edit, quality over count.
---
# EXTERNAL CRAFT BENCHMARK
The current architecture matches useful established interactive-narrative principles:
branch where the difference matters.
reconverge where production value is stronger than additional divergence.
distinguish rerouting choices from defining choices.
use player expression and character connection rather than consequence quantity alone.
treat dialogue as game-system content rather than detached prose.
The repeating-diamond/compositional structure is appropriate for a project with substantial agency and finite production resources.
Accessibility architecture is consistent with common guidance around remappable controls, subtitle clarity, non-color-only communication, adjustable timing, manual/autosave, and independent audio controls.
---
# FINAL GO / NO-GO
GO:
canon.
story premise.
critical-path writing direction.
companions.
SOVEREIGN.
God King concept.
choice architecture.
route architecture.
open-world philosophy.
systems plan.
implementation roadmap.
vertical slice.
---
CONDITIONAL GO:
hybrid perspective.
full weapon catalogue.
full subregion catalogue.
150 side-quest ceiling.
200-NPC ceiling.
full crime system.
stealth expansion.
mounts.
full voice acting.
These require prototype or budget proof.
---
NO-GO:
full-scale content production before vertical-slice gates.
binary morality.
loot-affix bloat.
durability chores.
mandatory survival meters.
procedural main story.
map size as a KPI.
keeping weak dialogue merely to maintain line count.
---
# FINAL VERDICT
The master is now better after becoming smaller.
The old 100k-plus line milestone was useful as an exploration exercise but was not a quality achievement by itself.
Removing repetitive generated prose increased production value.
The document now functions more like a real game bible:
canon.
scene direction.
choice architecture.
world plan.
system contract.
roadmap.
QA contract.
content reservoir.
The design has credible 9/10-plus game potential.
It does not have a credible guarantee of a 9/10-plus game.
That difference matters.
The next decisive evidence must come from the vertical slice.
If movement, Aldric, Elara, one living Oakhaven slice, one consequence chain, one companion state change, and one farming loop are genuinely fun together, the project deserves aggressive expansion.
If they are not, expanding the document or map would be the wrong response.
---
# END FINAL WHOLE-MASTER COLD REVIEW
# FINAL DESIGN REFINEMENT PATCH — HIGHEST AUTHORITY
Status: HIGHEST-AUTHORITY DESIGN PATCH.
This section supersedes any lower-precedence instruction that conflicts with it.
Purpose: resolve the final issues identified by independent reviews without reopening the central plot.
Changes:
strengthen Kaelen as a person.
protect genuinely low-stakes fun.
make Root mechanically distinctive.
make Story+ structurally asymmetric.
lock launch scope to a buildable target.
protect the revised opening motivation.
---
# A — OPENING MOTIVATION CONTRACT
The final prologue beginning with "Before the Ground" and the Chapter 1 "Road Ledger" scene are canonical.
Kaelen's initial motivation is not "save Aethelgard."
His opening goals are:
survive.
find Flight 707.
find other passengers.
understand why no wreckage or bodies remain.
reach Ironhold's Arrival Registry.
Kaelen's investment in Oakhaven grows through:
shelter.
information.
reciprocity.
Elara.
visible ordinary people.
the blocked route he personally needs.
Aldric.
the Source Key recognition.
The player must be allowed to understand why Kaelen takes each next step.
No chapter may rely on "because this is the main quest" as Kaelen's only motive.
---
# B — KAELEN PERSONAL IDENTITY BIBLE
Status: CANONICAL CHARACTER LAYER.
Purpose: make Kaelen recognizable even in a scene where Root Access, programming, and world-saving are absent.
---
## Kaelen's baseline personality
Observant.
Dry rather than constantly sarcastic.
Helpful when the problem has a clear shape.
Defensive when responsibility becomes accusation.
Bad at admitting fear before it becomes exhaustion.
Tends to solve before listening when stressed.
Becomes more talkative when sleep-deprived.
Can be petty.
Can be selfish.
Can be wrong about ordinary things.
Does not need to be the funniest person in the room.
---
## Kaelen's ordinary tastes
Likes very strong coffee even when it is objectively bad.
Misses cheap late-night instant noodles more than expensive Earth food.
Likes food with too much salt.
Dislikes pears.
This creates a harmless recurring disagreement with Lyra's pear-tea notes.
Hates wet socks with unreasonable intensity.
Prefers old comfortable clothes to impressive clothes.
Keeps broken objects longer than necessary because he believes he will repair them.
Likes rain when he is indoors.
Dislikes decorative cushions because nobody is allowed to sit on them correctly.
---
## Kaelen's Earth habits
Used to rotate the same three mugs until one broke.
Worked too late and then pretended the schedule was intentional.
Kept browser tabs open for weeks.
Listened to old instrumental game and film soundtracks while debugging.
Played strategy games badly but confidently.
Could cook exactly four meals reliably.
Used public transit whenever possible because driving stressed him.
Collected transit cards, ticket stubs, and other useless proof that he had been somewhere.
This gives him a reason to keep the Flight 707 fragment beyond plot utility.
---
## Kaelen's hobby
Kaelen likes sketching maps and room layouts badly.
He does not think of it as art.
He draws to understand spaces.
Kaito thinks the maps are terrible.
Kaelen insists they are diagrams.
This gives Kaelen a nontechnical activity that can appear in camps, journals, and environmental moments.
---
## Kaelen's embarrassing trait
He reads warning labels aloud when nervous.
He claims this is because warnings are useful.
Elara eventually recognizes it as a stress tell.
---
## Kaelen's irrational dislike
He dislikes wind chimes.
He does not have a tragic reason.
He simply hates the sound.
Oakhaven has several.
This is allowed to remain meaningless.
---
## Kaelen's selfish wants
He wants to know whether Earth still exists.
He wants to know whether anyone from Flight 707 survived.
He wants one day in which nobody asks him to make a system-level decision.
He occasionally wants to leave Aethelgard even after he loves people there.
He can want home without making Aethelgard less real.
He can resent being needed.
He can enjoy being needed and then feel guilty about enjoying it.
---
## Kaelen's fear
His deepest practical fear is not death.
It is making one irreversible decision because he was the only person capable of making it, then discovering capability was the only reason anyone allowed him to decide.
This connects to the theme but remains personal.
---
## Kaelen's petty failures
He loses small objects.
He forgets names when concentrating on systems.
He overestimates how obvious his explanations are.
He gives directions using landmarks nobody else noticed.
He is terrible at judging how much food a group needs.
He sometimes fixes the technically interesting part of a problem before the urgent boring part.
Companions may call him on this.
---
## Kaelen's humor range
Deadpan remains one mode.
Other modes:
bad analogy.
deliberately overtechnical answer.
unexpected enthusiasm.
self-deprecation.
silent facial reaction.
petty complaint.
genuine laughter.
occasional failed joke.
He must not answer every absurdity with the same short dry cadence.
---
## Kaelen and Mira
Do not make Mira a prize.
Do not define their exact relationship earlier than needed.
Memories can support:
closeness.
unfinished conflict.
professional history.
affection.
regret.
The uncertainty should concern what they meant to each other, not whether Mira mattered.
Kaelen's desire to find her or understand what happened to her must periodically re-enter the story.
---
## Kaelen dialogue test
Before a major Kaelen line ships, ask:
Could Elara say this unchanged.
Could Seraphina say this unchanged.
Could a generic sarcastic RPG protagonist say this unchanged.
If yes, rewrite when the scene matters.
---

At least half of designated low-stakes scenes remain exactly what they appear to be.

or small personal stakes.

# D — ROOT MECHANICAL IDENTITY
Status: CANONICAL CORE-GAME DIFFERENTIATOR.
Purpose: make Aethelgard mechanically recognizable rather than merely a strong 2D action RPG.
Root is not "magic spell category."
Root is constrained interaction with system directives and relationships.
---
## Root verbs
TRACE.
Read a target's known properties, dependencies, directives, and recent failures.
Low corruption.
Common exploration/combat utility.
---
INTERRUPT.
Temporarily suspend a valid process or directive.
Examples:
pause turret cycle.
stop a closing gate.
interrupt summon command.
freeze a moving hazard.
Short duration.
Moderate cost.
---
REDIRECT.
Change a valid target, priority, path, or permitted recipient inside an existing directive.
Examples:
summon protects wrong target.
security process attacks Fracture instead of civilians.
hazard vents toward empty arena segment.
Higher corruption than TRACE.
---
ISOLATE.
Quarantine one corrupted process from another.
Examples:
separate boss buff from source node.
stop Fracture spread through bridge.
prevent one memory-state conflict from infecting adjacent system.
Often creates a physical gameplay window.
---
RESTORE.
Return a nonperson system/object to a known earlier valid state.
Examples:
restore bridge segment.
rebuild platform.
restore broken elevator logic.
restore cover.
Cannot freely restore persons.
Person restoration remains major story/medical/legal content.
---
LINK.
Create a temporary dependency between compatible systems.
Examples:
power broken door from nearby shrine.
link enemy shield to hazard.
link platform movement to attack cycle.
High creativity potential.
Strong corruption if abused.
---
REWRITE.
Late-game, narrow, high-risk modification to deeper logic.
Requires sufficient Source authorization.
Always shows consequence warning.
Often irreversible.
Person-directed REWRITE is never a casual combat action.
---
## Root unlock progression
Early game:
TRACE.
limited REDIRECT.
limited INTERRUPT.
Mid game:
ISOLATE.
RESTORE for nonperson systems.
LINK.
Late game:
broader cross-system operations.
limited REWRITE.
Source fragments increase authorization breadth rather than simply damage.
---
## Root combat examples
Enemy has DIRECTIVE: PROTECT CAPTAIN.
Player redirects protection toward nearest conscious unit.
Enemy may shield a civilian or another enemy.
---
Boss shield depends on three relay nodes.
Player can:
destroy nodes conventionally.
TRACE dependency.
LINK two nodes so damage propagates.
ISOLATE one node from shield network.
Different builds solve same problem differently.
---
Summoner creates drones.
TRACE reveals drones obey RETURN_IF_MASTER_HEALTH_LOW.
Player can damage summoner and REDIRECT return location into arena hazard.
---
Boss windup triggers arena crusher.
Player can INTERRUPT crusher.
Or LINK crusher trigger to boss heavy attack.
Root creates systemic opportunity rather than canned quick-time interaction.
---
## Root exploration examples
Collapsed bridge:
physical repair quest.
RESTORE temporary segment.
find alternate route.
ask regional workers.
Every option remains valid.
---
Locked facility:
find key.
earn permission.
locate maintenance route.
TRACE authorization chain.
REDIRECT a valid maintenance token.
Root is an option, not universal lockpick.
---
Moving Wastes road:
TRACE route rule.
LINK road anchor to visible landmark temporarily.
Kaito can solve through mapping instead.
---
## Root personhood rule
Ordinary enemies may be clearly nonperson processes.
Named people, uncertain consciousnesses, restored minds, process-persons, and ambiguous targets cannot be casually rewritten like objects.
The UI visibly distinguishes:
OBJECT.
AUTOMATION.
CREATURE.
UNCERTAIN PROCESS.
PERSON.
UNKNOWN.
Uncertainty is mechanically important.
---
## Root consequence categories
Corruption.
social reaction.
system instability.
legal/reputation reaction.
future state.
resource cost.
Some Root actions have no moral consequence because turning on a broken lift should not become an ethics exam.
---
## Root creativity rule
At least one encounter per major region should contain a Root interaction that playtesters discover rather than receive as a tutorial prompt.
At least one boss per act should support a nonobvious Root tactic.
The best Root solutions should produce player stories.
---
## Root anti-gimmick rule
Do not paint every editable object glowing blue.
TRACE/observation, environment, companion hints, and player learning should reveal possibilities.
Accessibility option may increase Root-interactable visibility.
---

## Story+ asymmetry rules
Some routes may be two hours.
Some may be forty minutes.
Equal legitimacy does not mean equal runtime.
Some routes can contain no boss.
Some can contain one major rescue encounter.
Some can have no hearing.
Some can begin with the crisis already underway.
Some can end before the player thinks the problem is solved.
Some can have the apparent solution in the first third and explore consequences afterward.
The player should recognize the route by what they are doing, not only what NPCs are saying.

SOVEREIGN.
God King.

Approximately twenty-eight to thirty-two substantial explorable subregions/spaces across the whole launch game, plus hubs and small secrets.

Target approximately seventy strong side quests.

launch target approximately one hundred to one hundred forty active scheduled residents across all regions.
The ~200 pool remains available for expansion, Story+, and density tuning.
Crowd/background characters can use lighter nonpersistent presentation where appropriate.
---
## Companion scope
Keep all eight major companions.
Reason:
they are central to narrative identity and replayability.
Scope control comes from:
one active field companion.
compact progression.
curated gear.
selective state queries.
not reducing the cast.
Recruitment is staggered so eight AI/content systems are not introduced at once.
---
## Weapon scope
Launch target:
five excellent weapon families plus shield/off-hand and Root system.
Candidate core:
Longsword.
Greatblade.
Twin Blades or Dagger.
Spear.
Hammer or Arc Blade.
Final selection comes from prototypes.
Other weapon concepts remain expansion candidates.
Do not ship a sixth family until the first five feel distinct.
---
## Enemy scope
Do not create six to ten wholly unique base families for every region.
Launch target:
approximately twenty-eight to thirty-six base enemy families across the entire game.
Regional identity comes from:
variants.
behaviors.
Fracture states.
equipment.
directives.
environment.
elite mutations.
A Wastes variant can share skeleton/logic with another family while playing differently.
---
## Boss production scope
Target approximately twelve to fourteen fully bespoke major-boss production packages.
Additional named confrontations may use:
elite rigs.
shared skeletal bases.
arena transformations.
noncombat resolution.
multi-stage encounters without unique full asset sets.
Examples:
Obedience/Efficiency/Mercy do not all require separate full-scale boss productions.
Mirror aspects may share production foundations.
Named does not automatically mean a new months-long boss pipeline.
Optional superboss launch target:
two to four.
More can arrive later.
---
## Story+ scope
Every ending retains a unique Story+ signature crisis concept.
A single playthrough only loads the achieved route.
Launch does not require twenty-seven equally enormous postgames.
Route runtime can vary.
Shared infrastructure and transformed base-world spaces are reused intelligently.
---
## Minigame/activity scope
Launch target:
one or two genuinely good signature activities per region at most.
Regional flavor beats minigame count.
Do not build twenty shallow systems.
---
## Systems deferred from launch unless prototypes/budget prove value
Full crime/wanted simulation.
deep systemic stealth.
mounts/vehicles.
full romance suite.
full voice acting.
large housing decoration.
photo mode.
additional weapon families.
large-scale procedural events.
These are not forbidden forever.
They are not allowed to steal resources from core quality.
---
## Voice scope
Canonical writing assumes text-first support.
If voice budget is partial, priority:
main critical path.
major companion scenes.
SOVEREIGN.
God King.
major bosses.
major Story+ scenes.
Ambient and Tier C can remain text with expressive sound.
Never cut essential state reactivity merely because full voice coverage is expensive.
---
## Base-game duration philosophy
Do not design toward a mandatory hour count.
Critical path should be finishable without consuming the content reservoir.
A player who explores should see substantially more.
Completionism should be possible but not required for narrative understanding.
The game must respect players who want:
main story.
main + companions.
deep exploration.
multiple replays.
---
## Scope expansion trigger
Reservoir content may move into launch only when all are true:
vertical slice passes.
combat is fun.
one full region feels alive.
save/state tests are stable.
performance budget is healthy.
existing content density is not repetitive.
adding the content improves player experience more than polishing existing content.
If any condition fails, polish wins.
---
## Scope cut rule
Cut/merge content when:
two quests perform the same emotional function.
two NPCs perform the same world function without meaningful distinction.
a subregion has no unique activity/story/traversal role.
a weapon lacks distinct feel.
a boss exists mainly to satisfy a boss count.
a system creates more menu friction than play.
Cut content returns to reservoir rather than being treated as failure.
---
## Ten-year vision rule
The ten-year plan is allowed to remain enormous.
Version 1 is not required to contain ten years of ideas.
The long-term master protects future possibility.
The launch scope protects the first game.
Both can coexist.
---
# G — FINAL "DO NOT ADD MORE LORE" RULE
Until the vertical slice is playable:
no new major faction.
no new major region.
no new cosmic layer.
no new final antagonist.
no new ending axis.
no ninth companion.
New ideas may be logged in a parking-lot document.
They do not enter canonical launch scope.
Work now moves from invention to proof.
---
# END FINAL DESIGN REFINEMENT PATCH
